statement: PREFIX-RANK STATE BOUND (repair of S0046). Let W be an integer m x n matrix with |W_ji| <= M, let W_k be its first k columns, r_k = rank_Q(W_k) >= 1, and S_k = {W_k a : a in {0,1}^k}. Then |S_k| <= min(2^k, (2Mk+1)^{r_k}).

label: S0052
statement: LEMMA (touched-column bound). Let W, L, E be integer m x p matrices with W = L + E, max|L_ij| <= M, rank_Q(L) <= r, and E_ij = 0 outside a column set C with |C| = c. Then #{Wx : x in {0,1}^p} <= min(2^p, (2Mp+1)^r * 2^c). PROOF: (1) Let rows I (|I| = rank L <= r) be a Q-basis of the row space of L, and R = L_I. Each row of L is a Q-combination of rows of R, so Lx = Lambda(Rx) for a fixed rational matrix Lambda. (2) Rx is an integer vector with entries bounded by Mp in absolute value, so #{Rx} <= (2Mp+1)^r. (3) Ex = E_{.,C} x_C depends only on x_C, so #{Ex} <= 2^c. (4) Wx = Lambda(Rx) + Ex is a function of the pair (Rx, x_C), so #{Wx} <= #{(Rx, x_C)} <= (2Mp+1)^r 2^c. The trivial bound 2^p is also an upper bound. QED. Consequence: the thresholded prefix states [W_j x >= t_j] are functions of Wx, so the same bound holds for state counts. Asymptotically, with r = o(p / log p), M constant and c <= (1-delta) p, the state count is at most 2^{(1-delta+o(1)) p}. Correction of earlier record S-b2c28a4a0d: its claim that the saving disappears once k is a constant fraction of n is not established; this lemma bounds it only through c.

label: S0054
statement: LEMMA (M-free rank bound on bottom patterns). Let W in Q^{m x n} have rank r, t in Q^m, and P(W,t) = {(1[W_j.x >= t_j])_{j<=m} : x in {0,1}^n}. Then |P(W,t)| <= min(2^n, sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i)). PROOF. Factor W = U V with U in Q^{m x r}, V in Q^{r x n} (rank r). Put z = Vx. Then W_j.x = U_j.z, so the pattern is a function of z in the finite set Z = {Vx : x in {0,1}^n} subset of Q^r. Let D = {U_j.z - t_j : j, z in Z} and delta = min{|d| : d in D, d != 0} > 0 (finite set of rationals; if D = {0} there is no sign change to track). Choose eps in Q with 0 < eps < delta and t_j - eps not equal to U_j.z for all j and z in Z (finitely many exclusions). For z in Z: 1[U_j.z >= t_j] = 1[U_j.z > t_j - eps], because U_j.z >= t_j implies U_j.z > t_j - eps, and U_j.z < t_j implies U_j.z <= t_j - delta < t_j - eps. The hyperplanes H_j = {z : U_j.z = t_j - eps} avoid Z, so each z in Z lies in an open cell of the arrangement {H_j} in R^r, and the pattern is determined by that cell. Distinct patterns come from distinct cells. Rows U_j = 0 give constant sign and define no hyperplane; dropping them leaves m' <= m hyperplanes. A central fact (Buck 1943; Zaslavsky 1975): an arrangement of m' affine hyperplanes in R^r has at most sum_{i<=r} C(m',i) <= sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) cells. Hence |P| <= sum_{i<=r} C(m,i). Also |P| <= 2^n trivially. QED. COROLLARY: sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) <= (m+1)^r = 2^{r log2(m+1)}, so for m = n^alpha and r(alpha log2 n + 1) <= (1-eps) n the number of bottom patterns is at most 2^{(1-eps)n}, for every weight size M.

structure.lemma: CLIPPED EXCEPTIONAL-ROW DP. W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B; normal rows N with rank r and row basis R, A = W_R; k exceptional rows X with block E = W_X. For a prefix length p let L+_q(p) = sum_{i>p} max(0,E_qi), L-_q(p) = sum_{i>p} min(0,E_qi), and clip z_q to c_q(z,p) = clamp(z_q, t_q - L+_q(p) - 1, t_q - L-_q(p)). Then (a) #SAT f is computed exactly by the DP over keys (y_p, c(z_p,p)), where y_p = A x_{<=p} and z_p = E x_{<=p}; (b) the number of keys at step p is at most min{ 2^p, prod_k(||A_k^{<=p}||_1+1) * prod_q(L+_q(p)-L-_q(p)+2) }. Proof of (a): for any future suffix delta in [L-,L+] the indicator [z_q+delta_q >= t_q] is unchanged by clamping z_q, so keys with equal (y, clipped z) have identical future weights; the transition commutes with clipping by the same argument at p+1. Proof of (b): y-coordinates lie in integer intervals of length ||A_k^{<=p}||_1; clipped z-coordinates lie in an integer interval of length L+-L-+1. Scope: exact for any integer W; the bound improves the constant over (nB+1)^{r+k} but gives no exponent saving for fixed k, and nothing for full-rank W (G0001(iii) stays open).

label: S0081
statement: LEMMA W (window + state bound, repairs CLAIM 1). Setting as in the record: W = [C A ; E] with A in Z^{r x n}, |A|,|W| <= B, E in Z^{k x n}, thresholds t_j, weights v_j >= 1, V = sum_j v_j, prefix length p, suffix sums L-_j(p) = sum_{i>p} min(W_ji,0), L+_j(p) = sum_{i>p} max(W_ji,0). PROOF. (1) Decision rule: after reading x_1..x_p with partial sum s_j, gate j is decided true if s_j + L-_j(p) >= t_j, decided false if s_j + L+_j(p) < t_j, and undecided otherwise. Future sums lie in [s_j+L-_j, s_j+L+_j], so a decided gate keeps its value for every suffix; the DP is exact (dropping decided gates loses no information). (2) Window: a gate undecided at p has s_j in [t_j - L+_j(p), t_j - L-_j(p)), an interval of length L+_j - L-_j = sum_{i>p}|W_ji| <= (n-p)B, so it has at most (n-p)B+2 integer values. Thus the clamp of the record is not needed: undecided values are already windowed. (3) Normal rows: for j in N, s_j = U_j . y with y = A x_{<=p} in Z^r, |y_i| <= pB, so the undecided normal values are a function of y: at most (2pB+1)^r possibilities. (4) The key is (cnt, f(y), (undecided K-values)), cnt in {0..V}. Hence the number of keys at prefix p is at most (V+1) (2pB+1)^r ((n-p)B+2)^k. (5) Running time: O(n m (V+1)(2nB+3)^{r+k}) exact arithmetic, so 2^{(1-eps)n} poly whenever (r+k) log2(2nB+3) <= (1-eps) n - O(log n). SCOPE: exact for any r, k, B, V; a saving only for r+k = O(n/log n). It does not close G0001(i), G0001(iii), G0003 or G0006; it shrinks the constant of CLAIM 1 from (nB+3)^k to ((n-p)B+2)^k and corrects the claim that unclipped values are unbounded. Repair of the refuted note: the 'unclipped values reach (2pB+1)^k' remark is withdrawn.

statement: Proof. For j in [m] and x in {0,1}^p: W_{j,<=p} . x = sum_{i<=p} (sum_k U_{jk} A_{ki}) x_i + sum_{i<=p} E_{ji} x_i = sum_k U_{jk} y_k + sum_{i in T cap [p]} E_{ji} x_i, where y = A_{<=p} x_{<=p} in Z^r. So the whole state vector is a function of the pair (y, x restricted to T cap [p]). Since |y_k| <= B p, y takes at most (2Bp+1)^r values; the restriction takes at most 2^{|T cap [p]|} values. Counting pairs gives the bound; the bound 2^p is trivial. Since p <= n, (2Bp+1)^r <= (2Bn+1)^r, and 2^s (2Bn+1)^r = 2^{s + r log2(2Bn+1)} <= 2^{(1-eps) n} under the stated condition. Sanity check: with s = 0 (pure rank r) it recovers the rank-r state bound. Scope: exact, for any m; T is one fixed set for the whole matrix, not per row. Not covered: per-row k-sparse E whose supports together cover all columns (the union support is then all n columns, so s = n).

structure.lemma: Structured-support state lemma. Let n, m, r >= 1, B >= 0 be integers. Let A be an r x n integer matrix with entries in [-B, B], U an arbitrary m x r integer matrix, and E an m x n integer matrix whose nonzero columns all lie in a fixed set T of size s. Put W = UA + E. For a prefix length p <= n, the prefix state of x in {0,1}^p is the vector (W_{j,<=p} . x_{<=p}) over j in [m]. Claim: the number of distinct prefix states over x in {0,1}^p is at most min(2^p, (2Bp+1)^r * 2^{|T cap [p]|}). Consequently, if s + r*log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-eps) n, every prefix state count is at most 2^{(1-eps) n}.
structure.proved_step: Proof. For j in [m] and x in {0,1}^p: W_{j,<=p} . x = sum_{i<=p} (sum_k U_{jk} A_{ki}) x_i + sum_{i<=p} E_{ji} x_i = sum_k U_{jk} y_k + sum_{i in T cap [p]} E_{ji} x_i, where y = A_{<=p} x_{<=p} in Z^r. So the whole state vector is a function of the pair (y, x restricted to T cap [p]). Since |y_k| <= B p, y takes at most (2Bp+1)^r values; the restriction takes at most 2^{|T cap [p]|} values. Counting pairs gives the bound; the bound 2^p is trivial. Since p <= n, (2Bp+1)^r <= (2Bn+1)^r, and 2^s (2Bn+1)^r = 2^{s + r log2(2Bn+1)} <= 2^{(1-eps) n} under the stated condition. label: S0091
statement: CLAIMED (R0953). ROW-OUTLIER RANK LEMMA (row-sparse case of G0001(i)). Setting: W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B_W; t in Z^m; T in Z; a set K of exceptional rows with |K| = k; every j outside K has W_j = U_j A with U_j in Z^r and A in Z^{r x n}, |A_ic| <= B_A (rows of A fixed, the same for all normal rows). Statement: N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} can be computed exactly by a DP whose number of states after reading x_1..x_p is at most (k+1)(2pB_A+1)^r ((n-p)B_W+1)^k. Hence N is computed in time poly(n,m) (k+1) (2nB_A+1)^r (nB_W+1)^k. In particular N is computed in time 2^{(1-eps)n} poly(n,m) whenever r log2(2nB_A+1) + k log2(nB_W+1) + log2(k+1) <= (1-eps) n. PROOF. Key after prefix p: (cnt, y = A x_{<=p}, sorted tuple of (q, s_q) for q in K undecided at p, with exact partial sums s_q = W_{q,<=p}.x_{<=p}). cnt in {0..k} counts exceptional rows already decided TRUE. A row q is decided at p when its future range [minfut, maxfut] lets it be fixed; decided-FALSE rows contribute nothing. Transition: reading x_{p+1} adds A_{.,p+1} to y and W_{q,p+1} to each undecided s_q, then decides rows. Exactness: the future count depends only on the key, because (i) decided exceptional rows are absorbed into cnt; (ii) for an undecided q the future outcome depends only on s_q; (iii) a normal row j satisfies W_j.x = U_j.(A x), so at the end it is decided by U_j.y_n >= t_j with y_n = y_p + A x_{>p}, which depends only on the key and the future bits. Counting: y lies in [-pB_A, pB_A]^r, so (2pB_A+1)^r values; for each q in K the entry is absent or s_q lies in the integer window [t_q - maxfut_q(p), t_q - minfut_q(p) - 1] of size maxfut - minfut <= (n-p)B_W, so at most (n-p)B_W+1 options; cnt gives k+1. Multiplying gives the bound. The DP is exact by (i)-(iii). SCOPE AND LIMITS: (a) needs k log2(nB_W+1) + r log2(2nB_A+1) <= (1-eps)n, so it covers rank r on all but k = o(n/log n) rows, not full-rank W (k=0, r=n fails). (b) Entry-spread error across all columns is NOT covered (G0012, G0013 remain open). (c) Whether hard m = n^alpha THR o THR families have all but o(n/log n) gates in an o(n/log n)-dim row span is open (G0002, G0006). (d) Numerical support: cm-8dc4437721694664 (360 exact cases, 0 mismatches). Reviewer: this may be judged a combination of known DP and rank techniques; confirms_closure is not assumed. Obligation closed: G0001 row-sparse subcase only.

label: S0094
statement: PREFIX-RANK STATE LEMMA (general, no factorisation). Let W be an m x n integer matrix with all entries in [-L, L], L >= 1. For 1 <= p <= n let rho_p = rank over Q of the prefix block W[:, 1..p]. Then the number of distinct prefix states {W[:,1..p] x : x in {0,1}^p} is at most min(2^p, (2Lp+1)^{rho_p}). PROOF: choose rho_p linearly independent rows R (a rho_p x p integer matrix) of the prefix block. Every other row of the prefix block is a rational combination of R, row_j = sum_i lambda_{ji} R_i, with lambda fixed by W and independent of x. So W_j,<=p x = sum_i lambda_{ji} (R_i x), and the whole state is a function of R x in Z^{rho_p}. Each entry of R x lies in [-Lp, Lp], a set of 2Lp+1 integers, so at most (2Lp+1)^{rho_p} values. The bound 2^p is trivial. Consequence: if rho_p * log2(2Ln+1) <= (1-eps) n for every prefix that is used, the state count is at most 2^{(1-eps) n}. SCOPE: this is S0081 with the hypothesis A,U,E replaced by 'the prefix rank is small'; for W of total rank r it gives rho_p <= r. It does NOT help full-rank W (rho_p = p gives only the trivial bound), and it does not handle near-low-rank W = UA+E unless the rank of W itself is small.

The test uses only low-rank W, so it checks the bound only where it is nontrivial by construction; it does not test full-rank W.

label: S0097
statement: LEMMA D1 (exact linear prefix-state limit). Claim (a): A x = A y iff A t = 0 with t = x - y in {-1,0,1}^p. Every nonzero t in {-1,0,1}^p arises as x - y with x = max(t,0) and y = max(-t,0), both in {0,1}^p, and x != y. So x -> Ax is injective on {0,1}^p iff no nonzero such t lies in ker A. If rank A = p then ker A = 0, so N(A) = 2^p. Claim (b), lower bound: pick r columns S with A_S of rank r. A_S is injective on Q^r, so the 2^r vectors A x with x in {0,1}^S (zero outside S) are distinct. Claim (b), upper bound: pick r linearly independent rows R of A. Every row of A is a rational combination of R, so A = M R with M rational, hence Ax = M(Rx). Each entry of Rx lies in [-Bp, Bp], so N(A) <= #{Rx} <= (2Bp+1)^r. The 2^p bound is trivial. Consequence: any DP whose state is the linear prefix vector Ax has at least 2^{rank A} states, and full-rank prefix blocks give exactly 2^p states. The rank DP saves only when r log2(2Bp+1) < p. This identifies the exact limit of the linear-state method and corrects the earlier open reading of G0003: for linear states the full-rank case is settled negatively, so any saving must come from non-linear state (thresholds or clipping) or from a different decomposition.

label: S0105
statement: L-PROD: CLAIMED. Proof. (1) Rows of R form a Q-basis of the row space, so each row k satisfies A_k = sum_{i in R} c_{k,i} A_i with rational c_{k,i}. Hence (Ax)_k = sum_i c_{k,i} (A_R x)_i, so Ax is a function of A_R x. (2) Thus N(A) <= |{A_R x : x in {0,1}^p}|. (3) For each i in R, (A_i x) is an integer in [sum_j min(a_ij,0), sum_j max(a_ij,0)], an interval of length ||A_i||_1, so it takes at most 1 + ||A_i||_1 values. (4) The image A_R x lies in the product of these intervals, which gives the product bound. (5) ||A_i||_1 <= Bp gives (1+Bp)^r; 2^{(1-eps)p} follows from r log2(1+Bp) <= (1-eps) p. Exact check of the product bound: cm-aff77c8e13b14bc5 (248 instances, 0 failures, 136 tight).

structure.lemma: Sharpened row-product bound for linear prefix states. Let A be an integer m x p matrix with rank r >= 1, let B = max |a_ij|, and let N(A) = |{Ax : x in {0,1}^p}|. Let R be any set of r rows whose restrictions are linearly independent over Q. Then N(A) <= prod_{i in R} (1 + ||A_i||_1). Consequently N(A) <= min(2^p, (1+Bp)^r), and N(A) <= 2^{(1-eps)p} whenever r <= (1-eps) p / log2(1+Bp).

label: S0107
statement: CLAIMED. Proof of the rank bound: let E_R be E restricted to rows in R and E_C = E - E_R. The nonzero entries of E_C lie in columns of C, so rank(E_C) <= |C|. E_R has at most |R| nonzero rows, so rank(E_R) <= |R|. By subadditivity, rank(W) <= rank(P) + rank(E_R) + rank(E_C) <= r + |R| + |C|. The #SAT consequence uses the rank-r DP with a basis of rank(W) independent rows: the vector of clipped partial sums of the basis rows determines every other row's partial sum, because each row is a rational combination of the basis rows, so the DP is determinate and has at most (2Bn+1)^{rank W} states.

structure.lemma: Cover-rank lemma. Let W in Z^{m x n} with W = P + E, rank(P) <= r, and suppose every nonzero entry of E lies in a row indexed by R or a column indexed by C. Then rank(W) <= r + |R| + |C|. Consequence: exact #SAT of THR o THR with bottom matrix W is computed in time poly(m,n) (2Bn+1)^{rank W}, where B bounds |entries| of W, by the rank-r DP lemma applied with r := rank W. Saving 2^{(1-eps) n} iff r + |R| + |C| <= (1-eps) n / log2(2Bn+1).

structure.refuted_approach: G0014 reading 'rank(W') <= r + |R|' for a vertex-cover support of E. Refuted as stated: a nonzero entry of E in a column of C and a row outside R moves that row off the rank-r span of P, so rows outside R need not equal rows of P. The correct bound uses the whole cover.

label: S0110
statement: COROLLARY of S0108 (entrywise sparse error). Let W = UA + E in Z^{m x n} with |W_jl| <= B, rank_Q(UA) <= r, and let E have k nonzero entries supported on a column set S with |S| = s <= k. Then N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed exactly with at most 2^s (2Bn+1)^r reachable states per column step. PROOF. W agrees with UA outside the columns S, so the submatrix of W on the columns outside S has rank at most r. Apply S0108 with S as the free columns (after a column permutation). No correction term is needed, because S0108 is exact. SAVING: holds when k + r log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-eps) n. SCOPE: nnz(E) = O(n) with rank r = O(n / log(Bn)). Sparse E with superlinear nnz is not covered. This is bookkeeping on S0108, not new progress toward G0002 in full. Not reviewed; CLAIMED and open until another session reviews it.

structure.lemma: L1 (weight-free sign-pattern count, rank r). Let W in Q^{m x n} have rank r >= 1, t in Q^m, sigma(x) = (1[W_j . x >= t_j])_{j<=m}. Then |{sigma(x) : x in {0,1}^n}| <= min(2^n, sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i)). Proof: factor W = UA (U in Q^{m x r}, A in Q^{r x n}); Y = {Ax : x in {0,1}^n} is finite; delta = min |U_j . y - t_j| over y in Y with U_j . y != t_j (delta = 1 if none); s_j = t_j - delta/2. For y in Y, U_j . y >= t_j implies U_j . y > s_j, and U_j . y < t_j implies U_j . y <= t_j - delta < s_j, so sigma(x)_j = 1[U_j . y(x) > s_j] and no Y-point lies on any hyperplane {U_j . y = s_j}. Hence sigma(x) is the sign vector of a cell of the arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^r; distinct cells have distinct sign vectors; the arrangement has at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) cells (Buck 1943 / Zaslavsky). Zero rows U_j = 0 give constant signs and do not increase the count.
structure.proved_step: L1 as stated in the lemma field: a correct bound on distinct output vectors of THR layers of a rank-r linear form system, with exact proof as recorded in the lemma field. Scope: any W of rank r, any real thresholds t; it bounds output vectors, not DP states and not a #SAT running time.

label: S0112
statement: LEMMA P1 (candidate, unreviewed). Let W in Z^{m x n}, t in Z^m, r = rank_Q(W). Then |{(1[W_j.x >= t_j])_{j<=m} : x in {0,1}^n}| <= sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i). Proof sketch: (a) integrality: W_j.x - t_j is an integer, so W_j.x >= t_j iff W_j.x > t'_j with t'_j = t_j - 1/2, and no cube point lies on a hyperplane {W_j.x = t'_j}. (b) Factor W = U L with L in Q^{r x n} of full row rank. Then W_j.x - t'_j = U_j.(Lx) - t'_j, so the pattern is a function of y = Lx in R^r off the affine hyperplanes {U_j.y = t'_j}. (c) Distinct patterns lie in distinct regions of an arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^r (zero rows U_j = 0 give constant coordinates), and such an arrangement has at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) regions (Buck 1943 / Zaslavsky count; general position is the maximum).

structure.evidence: cm-33a193a148d94f21 (54 rows, n in {6,8,10}, m in {n,2n}, r in {1,2,3}, rank(W|-t) version: 0 violations). cm-db89a7a570874510 (72 cases, rank(W) version: 0 violations, max ratio 0.727). Exact check, EXPLORATORY only; the proof above is a sketch that needs reviewer checking of the Buck/Zaslavsky citation and of step (c).
structure.gap: P1 bounds the number of distinct bottom-layer patterns, NOT #SAT. #SAT = sum over realised patterns p of [top(p)=1] * N(p), N(p) = #{x in cube : pattern(x)=p}. No poly-time procedure for N(p) is given, so P1 does not close G0001(i) or G0001(iii) or G0013. Size comparison: the pattern bound is m^r-type, about n^{1.5 r} for m = n^1.5; the rank-r DP bound is (2Bn+1)^r, about n^{(c+1) r} for B = n^c. P1 is smaller only when c > 1/2, so it does not dominate the DP in general. Same 2^{(1-eps)n} regime only for r = o(n/log n).

label: S0113
statement: Cover-rank lemma (L2, CLAIMED by this session, unreviewed). Let W = P + E over Q, rank(P) <= r, and suppose every nonzero entry of E lies in a row indexed by R or a column indexed by C. Then rank(W) <= r + |R| + |C|. Proof: let E_R be E with the rows outside R zeroed and E_C = E - E_R. The nonzero rows of E_R lie in R, so rank(E_R) <= |R|. Each nonzero entry of E_C lies outside R-rows, hence in a C-column, so rank(E_C) <= |C|. Subadditivity of rank gives rank(W) <= rank(P) + rank(E_R) + rank(E_C) <= r + |R| + |C|. The lemma is exact and general; its proof is four lines. Exact check: cm-085a13b0ab7343eb (2000 random instances, m,n <= 7, 0 failures, 594 tight equalities).

structure.gap: Scope: the lemma says nothing about cost unless the perturbation support is small. It does not close G0001(i): the lemma needs |R|+|C| = o(n/log n) for the sparse error part, and no family of thr2 sharp_sat instances is shown to satisfy this. G0001(iii) (full rank) is untouched: for generic full-rank W the cover is C=all columns and the bound is vacuous. The DP corollary (rank-r DP, cm-2cd5c456ea174b3b) is a composition with the earlier CLAIMED rank-r lemma. Open: a structured instance family, or a concentration statement, with r + |R| + |C| <= (1-eps) n / log2(2Bn+1).

label: S0116
statement: L1 (sign-pattern bound, rank r): for W = UA in Q^{m x n} of rank r and any t in Q^m, the number of distinct vectors sigma(x) = (1[W_j . x >= t_j])_j over x in {0,1}^n is at most sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i). Proof: Y = {Ax : x in {0,1}^n} is finite; delta = min |U_j . y - t_j| over all j and all y with U_j . y != t_j (delta = 1 if none); s_j = t_j - delta/2. For y in Y, U_j . y >= t_j gives U_j . y > s_j, and U_j . y < t_j gives U_j . y <= t_j - delta < s_j, so sigma(x)_j = 1[U_j . y(x) > s_j]. No y in Y lies on any hyperplane U_j . y = s_j. Hence each sigma(x) is the sign vector of a region of an arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^r, and distinct regions have distinct sign vectors. Such an arrangement has at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) regions (Buck 1943). Zero rows of U give constant signs. Exact checks: cm-419a6daa690544c4 (n <= 14, m <= 40, r <= 3) and cm-a34f5fbef634467a (n = 14, r <= 4, weights up to 50): bound holds in all 9 configurations.

structure.gap: L1 is a counting bound on patterns. It is not an algorithm and does not close G0001(iii) or G0002. The missing step: compute N(p) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sigma(x) = p} for the poly(m) cells in time independent of the weight bit length (the rank-r DP has state count (2na+1)^r). The MITM check cm-419a6daa690544c4 is an exact correctness check at n <= 14 with no running-time claim, so it is not evidence of a speed-up.

label: S0123
statement: L3 (closed sign-pattern count, any dimension; repairs gap (f) of L2 without perturbation). Statement: for any d >= 0, m >= 0 and real affine functions f_1..f_m on R^d (f_j(x) = a_j.x - t_j, a_j = 0 allowed), the set P = { (1[f_j(x) >= 0])_{j<=m} : x in R^d } has |P| <= S(m,d) := sum_{i=0}^{d} C(m,i). PROOF by induction on m, all d at once. Base m=0: |P| = 1 = S(0,d). Base d=0: R^0 is one point, |P| <= 1 = S(m,0). Step m>=1, d>=1: let P' = patterns of f_1..f_{m-1} (the projection of P) and D = {p' in P' : both (p',0) and (p',1) lie in P}. Then |P| = |P'| + |D|. Case a_m = 0: f_m has constant sign, so D is empty and |P| = |P'| <= S(m-1,d) <= S(m,d). Case a_m != 0: H = {x : f_m(x) = 0} is an affine hyperplane isomorphic to R^{d-1}. Let p' in D be realised by x with f_m(x) >= 0 and y with f_m(y) < 0. Put z = (1-s)x + s y with s = f_m(x)/(f_m(x)-f_m(y)) in [0,1); then f_m(z) = 0, so z in H. Each f_j (j<m) is affine, so f_j(z) = (1-s) f_j(x) + s f_j(y). If p'_j = 1, both terms are >= 0, so f_j(z) >= 0; if p'_j = 0, both are < 0, so f_j(z) < 0. Hence z in H realises p' under the closed convention, so D lies in the pattern set of the m-1 restricted functions on H = R^{d-1}, and by induction |D| <= S(m-1,d-1). Therefore |P| <= S(m-1,d) + S(m-1,d-1) = S(m,d) by Pascal's rule C(m-1,i)+C(m-1,i-1) = C(m,i). QED. COROLLARY (rank r): if the bottom weights are W_j = U_j.A with U_j in Z^r and A an r x n integer matrix, then the bottom vector (1[W_j.x >= t_j])_j over x in {0,1}^n takes at most S(m,r) <= (m+1)^r values (subsets of [m] of size <= r inject into {0..m}^r by sorting and zero-padding). No general position, cell perturbation or half-open convention is needed, because the argument works with the closed sets directly. Numerical check: cm-5005f106b06d4a2d (exhaustive grid, m=2..5, coefficients and thresholds in {-1,0,1}; no violation).

label: S0129
statement: LEMMA L3 (sign-pattern bound, weight-free, rank r). Let W in Z^{m x n} have rank r over Q, t in Z^m, and for x in {0,1}^n put sigma(x)_j = [W_j . x >= t_j] in {0,1}^m. Then |{sigma(x) : x in {0,1}^n}| <= sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i). PROOF. Choose r linearly independent rows B of W; every row satisfies W_j = C_j B with C_j in Q^r. Put s = Bx in Z^r. Then W_j . x - t_j = C_j . s - t_j. Let D >= 1 be a common denominator of all C_j, so C_j . s - t_j lies in (1/D) Z for s in Z^r. Set tau_j = t_j - 1/(2D). Then C_j . s - tau_j lies in (1/D)Z + 1/(2D), which never equals 0, so sigma(x)_j = [C_j . s > tau_j] and no lattice point lies on any hyperplane H_j = {s : C_j . s = tau_j}. Hence sigma(x) is the sign vector of the cell of the affine arrangement {H_1..H_m} in R^r containing the point Bx. The number of cells of an arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^r is at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) (Buck 1943 / Zaslavsky 1975; induction R(m,r) <= R(m-1,r) + R(m-1,r-1), R(0,r) = R(m,0) = 1, which solves to the sum). QED. SCOPE: any integer W of rank r, any integer thresholds, any n; no weight-size assumption. The bound counts distinct SIGN PATTERNS of the full input x. It is not a bound on the number of DP states of a prefix-by-prefix dynamic program, and it does not bound the number of residual functions of a prefix.

structure.gap: L3 does not close G0001(iii), G0006 or G0002. The DP state after a prefix is the prefix vector s_P = B_P x_P in Z^r. Its future behaviour is determined by the residual function x_S -> sign(C s_P + W_S x_S - t), not by the sign pattern of s_P alone. Counting residual classes needs the arrangement of m 2^{n-k} hyperplanes in R^r, which gives (m 2^{n-k})^r, not the Buck bound, so the saving does not follow. The table is consistent with the lemma: log2(sum C(m,r))/n at m = n^{1.5}, r = d n/log n tends to d/2 only slowly (0.92 at n = 4096, d = 1). Open: a residual-class bound for prefixes, which is G0005's clipped-state question.

structure.evidence: The transition adds the next variable's weight, clips a gate only when remaining minimum or maximum forces its output, and merges only identical clipped states. Induction over prefix length proves multiplicity preservation and identical completion values. This repairs the correctness-invariant omission, but the claimed runtime saving still requires an active-gate bound.

label: S0227
statement:
statement_start: For integer-weight threshold-of-threshold circuits, merging prefixes with identical clipped signatures preserves the exact satisfying-assignment count.
statement: For C(x)=1[sum_j a_j y_j(x) >= T], with y_j(x)=1[sum_i w_ji x_i >= theta_j] and integer weights and thresholds, define a prefix signature at depth k by each bottom gate's status (forced 1, forced 0, or active), the exact partial sum for each active gate, and the top-level weighted sum of forced-1 gates. A gate is forced 1 when its partial sum plus the minimum possible remaining contribution is at least its threshold, and forced 0 when its partial sum plus the maximum possible remaining contribution is below its threshold. The dynamic program that extends prefixes by each next bit, recomputes statuses, merges equal signatures, and adds multiplicities returns the exact number of satisfying inputs.
proof: Induct on prefix length. The empty prefix is represented once. For an extension by bit b, add w_j,k+1*b to each active gate's partial sum and classify against the remaining suffix contributions. A previously forced gate remains forced to the same value because its new suffixes are a subset of the suffixes for which its value was already forced. If two prefixes have equal signatures, active gates have equal partial sums and hence equal outputs on every common suffix; forced gates have equal outputs by signature. Thus both prefixes induce the same circuit value for every common suffix. Merging them and summing multiplicities preserves the count of prefixes and all satisfying completions. At depth n all gate outputs are fixed, and accepting precisely when the resulting top-level weighted sum is at least T yields the exact count.

label: S0231
statement: statement: LEMMA (row-norm rank-after-deletion DP). Let W∈Z^{m×n}, C⊆[n], U=[n]\C, and let B_1,…,B_k be independent rows spanning the row space over Q of W[:,U]. Define L_l=Σ_{i∈U}|W_{B_l i}|. For f(x)=[Σ_j v_j[W_j·x≥t_j]≥T], #f is computable exactly in at most 2^{|C|}·poly(m,n)·∏_{l=1}^k(L_l+1) state-processing operations (arithmetic bit complexity additionally depends polynomially on input and intermediate bit lengths). Proof: Fix x_C. Process coordinates of x_U in any fixed order. At a prefix, store y_l=Σ_{i in prefix}W_{B_l i}x_i for each l, aggregating the number of prefixes at each vector y. Since x_i∈{0,1}, y_l lies between the sum of negative coefficients in that prefix and the sum of positive coefficients; hence it has at most 1+Σ_{i in prefix}|W_{B_l i}|≤L_l+1 possible integer values. Thus there are at most ∏_l(L_l+1) states at each layer, and the next-bit transition adds either zero or the next column vector. At the terminal layer each row W_j[:,U] is a rational linear combination of the spanning rows B_l, so W_j[:,U]·x_U is determined exactly by y. The fixed contribution W_j[:,C]·x_C is known, so every threshold gate and f is determined by the terminal state. Summing multiplicities of accepting terminal states counts all completions for this x_C; summing over all assignments x_C counts every x exactly once. There are |U|+1 layers and 2^{|C|} branches, giving the stated bound. If every selected basis row has coefficient absolute sum at most L, the state factor improves from (2a|U|+1)^k to (L+1)^k. This refines the state bound for the recorded rank-after-deletion gap; it does not imply a saving when these row norms or k are large.

statement: REPAIRED CLIPPED-THRESHOLD DP LEMMA. Let W=[P R] be an integer m-by-(l+k) matrix, with arbitrary integer thresholds t, output weights v, and target T, all given in binary. Define f(y,z)=[sum_j v_j [P_j.y+R_j.z>=t_j] >= T]. For each y in {0,1}^l let theta_j(y)=clip(t_j-P_j.y, lo_j, hi_j+1), where lo_j=sum_i min(R_ji,0) and hi_j=sum_i max(R_ji,0); let U={theta(y): y in {0,1}^l}. Then #f^{-1}(1) can be computed exactly in O(poly(L,m,l,k) * (2^l + 2^k |U|)) bit operations, where L is the total binary input length. Proof: For fixed y,j, R_j.z ranges over all z in {0,1}^k within [lo_j,hi_j]. If t_j-P_j.y <= lo_j, the gate is always true; if it is >= hi_j+1, it is always false; otherwise its threshold is exactly theta_j(y). Thus the suffix function depends on y only through theta(y). Enumerate all 2^l prefixes, accumulating their multiplicities by theta. For each distinct theta, enumerate all 2^k suffixes and evaluate the circuit, multiplying its satisfying count by the stored prefix multiplicity. This counts every pair (y,z) exactly once. All arithmetic operands have O(L+n+log m) bits (counts are at most 2^(l+k); sums have at most the input weight length plus this count length), so each operation has polynomial bit cost in L,m,l,k. The algorithm therefore has the stated bit bound. No family-level bound on |U| is implied.

statement: LEMMA (rank-r threshold-counting DP). Let W be an m-by-n integer matrix with |W_ji|<=B, let t_j be integers, v_j be nonnegative integers, and T an integer. If rank_Q(W)<=r, then the number of x in {0,1}^n satisfying sum_j v_j [W_j x>=t_j]>=T can be computed exactly in O(nm (nB+1)^r poly(L)) bit operations, where L is the input bit length. Proof: choose r linearly independent rows A of W. For each prefix length p, maintain a map from y=A x_[p] to the number of prefixes producing y. Initially the map has only y=0 with multiplicity 1. For the next column a_i, replace each state y by y and y+a_i, adding multiplicities when they coincide. By induction, each map entry is exactly the number of prefixes with that row-sum vector. Each coordinate of y is an integer sum of p terms of magnitude at most B, so there are at most (2pB+1)^r states (and at most 2^p). At p=n, every row W_j is a rational linear combination c_j A because rank(W)<=r; hence W_jx=c_j y. Evaluate the threshold predicate from y and sum multiplicities of accepting states. The transitions cost O(r) arithmetic per state; exact rational coefficients c_j are obtained by Gaussian elimination, with polynomial bit complexity in the input encoding. Thus the number of states is at most (2nB+1)^r, yielding the asserted bound. This lemma is restricted to rank at most r and does not imply a subexponential bound for unrestricted THR∘THR.
gap: This gives an exact algorithm for the rank-r core used by the column-deletion reduction; it does not bound the cost of finding a deletion set or establish that unrestricted THR∘THR instances have small rank after deletion.

label: S0001
statement: Occurrence-2 control lemma. Let G be a loopless cubic multigraph with vertex set V (clauses) and edge set E (variables). Let F_G be the positive CNF with one exactly-one (1-in-3) constraint per vertex on its three incident edges. Then the models of F_G are in bijection with the perfect matchings of G, via T -> T (the set of true edges). Proof: T satisfies the constraint at v iff exactly one edge of T is incident to v; this holds for all v iff T is a perfect matching. Loopless ensures no clause contains the same variable twice. Parallel edges are distinct variables and are handled by the same argument.

statement: statement: Parity-support equations for the arity-3 equality signature. Let A=[[a,b],[c,d]] be invertible over C, with columns u=(a,c), v=(b,d). The signature u⊗u⊗u+v⊗v⊗v is supported only on even Hamming weights iff a^3+b^3=0 and ac^2+bd^2=0; it is supported only on odd Hamming weights iff a^2c+b^2d=0 and c^3+d^3=0. Proof: expansion gives coordinates (000,001,010,011,100,101,110,111) equal to (a^3+b^3, a^2c+b^2d, a^2c+b^2d, ac^2+bd^2, a^2c+b^2d, ac^2+bd^2, ac^2+bd^2, c^3+d^3); imposing vanishing on the opposite parity gives precisely those equations.

statement: statement: Every invertible complex matrix A=[[a,b],[c,d]] satisfying the even-support equations a^3+b^3=0 and ac^2+bd^2=0 has the form b=zeta*a, c=eta*d, with a,d nonzero, zeta^3=-1, eta^2=-zeta, and eta!=zeta; conversely every such choice satisfies the equations and is invertible. Proof: if a=0 then b=0 from a^3+b^3=0, contradicting invertibility; likewise b=0 forces a=0. Set zeta=b/a, so zeta^3=-1. The second equation reduces to c^2+zeta*d^2=0. If d=0 then c=0, contradicting invertibility, so set eta=c/d; then eta^2=-zeta. The determinant is ad*(eta-zeta), so invertibility is equivalent to eta!=zeta. Conversely these equations and inequalities directly imply both parity equations and nonzero determinant. This closes only the parameter-classification subproblem; compatibility with transformed EXACT1_3 remains open.

statement: statement: Let A=[[a,b],[c,d]] be invertible over C. If the transformed ternary equality signature is supported only on odd Hamming weights, then the transformed EXACT1_3 signature has nonzero 000 and 111 coordinates and hence is not supported on a single parity class. Proof: odd support gives a^2*c+b^2*d=0 and c^3+d^3=0. The latter plus invertibility forces c,d nonzero. If a=0, then b^2*d=0 forces b=0, contradicting invertibility; similarly b=0 forces a=0. statement: For every finite set X, permutation δ:X→X with a_j cycles of length j, and integer m≥0, the number of δ-invariant subsets U⊆X with |U|=m equals [x^m]∏_{j≥1}(1+x^j)^{a_j}.
proof: Decompose X into its disjoint δ-orbits, which are exactly the cycles. If U is δ-invariant, then for every u∈U all iterates δ^k(u) lie in U, so the entire cycle containing u lies in U. Thus U is a union of cycles. Conversely every union of cycles is δ-invariant. For each length-j cycle, choosing it contributes x^j to the size-generating polynomial if included and 1 if excluded. Choices for distinct cycles are independent, so multiplying these factors gives a polynomial whose coefficient of x^m counts exactly the invariant unions of size m. Grouping equal-length cycles yields ∏_{j≥1}(1+x^j)^{a_j}.

statement: Let δ act on X with a_j cycles of length j, and C act on Y with c_j cycles of length j. The number of injective maps ψ:X→Y satisfying C∘ψ=ψ∘δ is ∏_{j≥1}(c_j)_{a_j} j^{a_j}, where (c)_a=c(c−1)…(c−a+1), interpreted as zero if a>c.
proof: If Cψ=ψδ, then for x on a δ-cycle of length j, C^jψ(x)=ψ(δ^j x)=ψ(x); injectivity implies the least positive C-period of ψ(x) is exactly j. Thus ψ maps each δ-cycle to a C-cycle of the same length. Distinct δ-cycles map to distinct C-cycles, since their images would otherwise overlap, contradicting injectivity. For each j, assign the a_j distinguishable δ-cycles injectively to ambient cycles in (c_j)_{a_j} ways. For each assignment, choose the image of a fixed representative on each δ-cycle in j ways; equivariance then determines the rest. The choices are independent. Conversely, every such assignment and phase choice defines an injective equivariant map. Multiplying gives the formula.

statement: Let X,Y be finite sets with |X|=m and |Y|=N≥m, and let δ be any permutation of X. Then Σ_{C∈Sym(Y)} |{ψ:X↪Y : C∘ψ=ψ∘δ}| = N!.
proof: Count pairs (C,ψ) satisfying the equation by first choosing ψ. There are (N)_m injections. For each ψ, the equation forces C(ψ(x))=ψ(δ(x)) for every x∈X, specifying C on ψ(X). The remaining N−m points can be permuted in (N−m)! ways. Thus the pair count is (N)_m(N−m)!=N!. This counts the same pairs as summing, over each C∈Sym(Y), its compatible injections ψ, proving the identity.

structure.lemma: L1 (time-invariant unrolling, exact). Let C be a circuit with s gates, inputs x in {0,1}^n, depth d(g) = 1 + max d(inputs of g) (inputs have depth 0), output gate o, D = max_g d(g). Define the time-invariant system with state sigma in {0,1}^s, sigma^0 = 0, and update sigma^{t}_g = op_g(val_a, val_b) where val reads x_i or sigma^{t-1}_h. Claim: for all t and all g with d(g) <= t, sigma^t_g = C_g(x). Proof by induction on t: t=0 vacuous (no gate has depth 0). Step t-1 -> t: a gate g with d(g) <= t has every input h with d(h) <= t-1, so sigma^{t-1}_h = C_h(x) by hypothesis, hence sigma^t_g = C_g(x). Corollary: sigma^D_o = C(x) after D steps, with D*s gate evaluations in total. L1' (time-dependent schedule, exact): at step t evaluate exactly the gates with d(g) = t; each gate is evaluated once, so s evaluations in total and the output is correct after D steps. Consequence: the two cost accountings differ by a factor D for uniform (time-invariant) updates, and agree for depth-scheduled updates.
structure.proved_step: L1 and L1' as stated in lemma: each is a complete induction on t over the gate depth; CLAIMED until a different session reviews it.

statement: L4 (stream order, exact, bookkeeping). Let C be a fan-in-2 circuit with s gates, and let pi list its gates once each. Consider the one-pass rule: on arrival, compute the gate from its two inputs read from value memory, with s value bits and no other state. This rule computes C correctly in s steps if and only if pi is a topological order of the gate DAG. Proof: if pi is topological, induction on position shows every arriving gate's inputs are already stored, so each value is correct and exactly s steps are used. If pi is not topological, some gate g arrives before one of its gate inputs h; when g arrives the slot of h is still empty, so the rule reads an undefined value. Status: CLAIMED, needs independent review. This is bookkeeping and closes no obligation.

The dispute turns on whether the graph model fixes the stream order (FB1 accounting) or lets the order be arbitrary. No measurement settles this; it is a model-definition question to be decided from the contract text on the remaining pages, with the open items G0002 a and b unchanged.

statement: L5 (arbitrary labelling, exact bookkeeping). Let C be an acyclic fan-in-2 circuit with s gates, labelled in any order. Rule: at each step, among the gates not yet computed whose gate inputs are all computed (inputs of the circuit count as computed), compute the one with the smallest label. Claim: the rule is never stuck, performs exactly s steps, and every computed value equals C at that gate. Proof: let D(g) be the longest path from an input to g, so D(g) is at least 1 for gates and every gate input of g has smaller D. Suppose some gate is uncomputed at a point where the rule is stuck, and pick an uncomputed gate g of minimum D. Its gate inputs have smaller D, so they are computed, so g is ready, a contradiction. Hence the rule runs until all s gates are computed. Each step evaluates one gate whose inputs already hold correct values, so each value is correct by induction on the step count. Status: CLAIMED, needs independent review. Bookkeeping: it closes no obligation and does not by itself settle K9-D4.

structure.gap: K9-D4 remains OPEN. L5 gives a time-invariant rule (fixed program, state of 2s bits) that uses exactly s gate evaluations for ANY label order, so the D*s overhead of L1 is not forced by time-invariance alone. What remains open: (a) whether readiness detection (about s label checks per step) is charged under FB1 accounting; (b) whether the rule can be made one-pass, since it needs random access to the description table; (c) whether the stream order can be fixed to be topological, which L4 shows is sufficient; (d) the worst-case cost of the ready-set scan is not yet measured, only the pop count. Items (a) and (b) are the model-definition question the dispute turns on.

statement: LEMMA (store-then-run one-pass rule, CLAIMED). Model: a fan-in-2 circuit C with s gates is presented as a stream of s records (g, op_g, in_g1, in_g2), in an arbitrary order (a permutation of gate labels), each record read once; inputs x are available by random access. Algorithm: (1) during the single pass, write each record into a table T indexed by g; each record costs O(1) update; (2) after the pass, run the L3 worklist on T with no further reads of the stream. Claim: the run returns val[g] = C(x)_g for every gate, performs exactly s pops and s pushes, and E <= 2s decrements, where E is the number of gate-to-gate edges. Proof: after the pass T is exactly the description of C under the relabelling g, so T is a fan-in-2 DAG description of C. L3's proof (i)-(iii) uses only that every gate-input edge is counted in ind, and that C is acyclic (so (iii) induction on a topological order exists); both hold. Hence the run is correct, with s pops and s pushes by L3. Cost: state O(s log s) bits (value bits plus indices and op codes per record); update O(1) per record; post-pass O(s + E) = O(s) operations with random access into T.

structure.gap: This does NOT close G0002(a). The state is O(s log s) bits, not O(s), because each gate's two input indices must be stored, so this is not a one-pass rule with O(s) state. Note also that L5's '2s bits' counts value and counter bits only; the queue and pointers need log s bits each, so L5 has the same state issue. Open: (a) whether a one-pass rule with O(s) state exists for arbitrarily ordered descriptions (the state bound this lemma does not reach); (b) whether O(s log s) state is within the cost model of any published transfer (G0002 b); (c) whether random access to T is charged under FB1 accounting (G0004 a); (d) the topological-order question (L4 'if' direction only). label: S0001
statement: Let F be a CNF on n variables whose primal graph has a supplied tree decomposition of width t with O(n) bags. Then F has a deterministic decomposable NNF of size n·2^{O(t)}. Proof: Convert the decomposition to a rooted nice tree decomposition with O(n) bags and width t. At each bag, use one gate for every assignment to its at most t+1 variables that satisfies all clauses assigned at that bag. For each bag assignment, the gate represents precisely the assignments to variables introduced in its subtree that extend the bag assignment and satisfy all clauses assigned in that subtree. At an introduce or forget node, connect gates to the child gates whose assignments agree on the shared variables; when a variable is forgotten, OR the child gates for its two values. These OR inputs represent disjoint assignments because they differ on the forgotten variable. At a join, AND the two child gates agreeing with the parent bag assignment; the children’s variables outside the bag are disjoint, so this AND is decomposable. The root ORs the accepting root-bag assignments; distinct assignments are disjoint. Induction up the decomposition proves that the root represents exactly the satisfying assignments of F. Each bag has at most 2^{t+1} states and each state has at most 2^{O(t)} local connections, so total size is O(n·2^{O(t)}). This is an upper bound for the stated CNF class and decomposition representation; it does not imply a bound for arbitrary perfect-matching graphs.

statement: For f = e_s^T M_1(x_1)...M_n(x_n) e_t over any field F, with M_i(x_i) = A_i + x_i B_i and variables read once in fixed order 1..n: the commutative image is identically zero iff the non-commutative f is zero. Proof: the non-commutative expansion is sum_S c_S w_S with w_S = prod_{i in S} x_i (increasing indices) and c_S = e_s^T Y_1...Y_n e_t, Y_i = B_i for i in S and A_i otherwise; the commutative monomials prod_{i in S} x_i are distinct for distinct S, so all c_S = 0 is equivalent to f = 0. Consequence: zero-testing a commutative fixed-order ROABP reduces to non-commutative ROABP zero-testing (Raz-Shpilka 2005, deterministic poly time).

statement: L1 (placement, from the LIT-9 definitions, fixed polynomials t1 >= 2n, t2 >= t1): boundary-MINK^{t1,t2} YES = {x : exists p, |p| <= n-2, U(p) outputs x within t1 steps} AND {x : no p with |p| <= n-log n outputs x within t2 steps}; NO = {x : no p with |p| <= n-2 outputs x within t2 steps}. The first YES conjunct is NP-type (witness p, poly-time check); the other YES conjunct and the NO condition are coNP-type. L2 (P=NP consequence): if P=NP then boundary-MINK^{t1,t2} is in P, hence in ioBPP, so boundary-MINK^poly not in ioBPP fails. L3 (randomized version): the rK condition 'exists p with Pr_r[U(p,r)=x within t steps] >= 2/3' is MA-type; under P=NP, PH = P and BPP is in Sigma_2 within PH, so boundary-MINrK^{t1,t2} is in P, hence in ioBPP. Hence by Thm 1.2, OWF exists => P != NP, re-derived from the definitions and not from the spec's summary.

Steps L1-L3 are proofs from the definitions, not from the paper's text; the reviewer should check L1 (the quantifier structure of boundary-MINK) and L3 (P=NP => PH=P and BPP in Sigma_2).

statement: S0004 (CLAIMED, not reviewed): the promise problem boundary-MINK^{t1,t2} lies in NP-and-coNP (YES = NP-type conjunct AND coNP-type conjunct; NO = coNP-type). Consequence: if boundary-MINK^{t1,t2} is not in P then P != NP, because P = NP would put NP-and-coNP into P. Since P is contained in ioBPP, the deterministic hypothesis (not in P) is weaker than the ioBPP hypothesis of Thm 1.2 (not in ioBPP), yet it still implies P != NP. It is a sufficient condition for P != NP, not a reduction of P vs NP: a lower bound for a promise problem in NP-and-coNP is at least as hard as separating P from NP-and-coNP.

statement: S0006 (CLAIMED, relativization barrier, by R0763): any proof of 'boundary-MINK^{t1,t2} not in P' that relativizes is impossible. Argument: relativize S0003/S0005. structure.lemma: LEMMA W (width-independence of the P != NP consequence). Fix polynomials 2n <= t1(n) <= t2(n) and any w(n) with 2 <= w(n) <= n. Define boundary-MINK^{t1,t2}_w: YES = {x in {0,1}^n : K^{t1}(x) <= n-2 and K^{t2}(x) > n-w(n)}; NO = {x in {0,1}^n : K^{t2}(x) >= n-1}. (i) YES and NO are disjoint. (ii) If P = NP then the promise problem is in P. (iii) Hence if boundary-MINK^{t1,t2}_w is not in P, then P != NP. PROOF. (i) Monotonicity: K^{t2}(x) <= K^{t1}(x) since t1 <= t2. On YES, K^{t2}(x) <= K^{t1}(x) <= n-2 < n-1, so x is not in NO. (ii) Write YES = A AND B with A(x) = exists p, |p| <= n-2, U(p) outputs x within t1(n) steps (an NP predicate: witness p, polynomial simulation since t1 is polynomial), and B(x) = NOT exists p, |p| <= n-w(n), U(p) outputs x within t2(n) steps (the complement of an NP predicate, so coNP). NO = C(x) = NOT exists p, |p| <= n-2, U(p) outputs x within t2(n) steps, a coNP predicate. Algorithm: output A(x) AND B(x). On YES inputs A and B hold. On NO inputs A fails: A would give a p with |p| <= n-2 outputting x within t1 <= t2 steps, contradicting C. So under P = NP (NP and coNP both in P) the algorithm is correct on all promise inputs and runs in polynomial time. (iii) Contrapositive of (ii). The width w enters only through B, and B is coNP for every w, so no constant or log-width restriction is needed for (iii). SCOPE: deterministic K only. The randomized rK version (delta fixed, threshold n - ceil(log(1/(1-delta))) - 2) gives the same conclusion: under P = NP, PH = P, and the rK predicates (exists p with Pr_r[U(p,r)=x within t] >= 2/3, or the complementary universal form) are in the PH levels Sigma_3 / Pi_3 with BPP inside PH, hence in P. statement: LEMMA M (width monotonicity; closes the strength sub-question of Q-30ff0b05e0). Let 2 <= w <= w' <= n and P_w = boundary-MINK^{t1,t2}_w as in LEMMA W. (i) YES_w is contained in YES_{w'}; NO does not depend on w. (ii) For every promise class C closed under restriction to sub-promises (P, ioBPP and the infinitely-often variants): if P_{w'} is in C then P_w is in C. Hence P_c not in C (constant c) implies P_{log n} not in C, so constant-width hardness is at least as strong as log-width hardness. PROOF. (i) n-w >= n-w', so K^{t2}(x) > n-w implies K^{t2}(x) > n-w'; hence x in YES_w gives x in YES_{w'}. NO is defined without w. (ii) Let M solve P_{w'} (accept YES_{w'}, reject NO, on the inputs required by C). Since YES_w union NO is contained in YES_{w'} union NO, M accepts YES_w and rejects NO on the same inputs, so M solves P_w with the same error and index set. QED. NOT CLAIMED: that OWF implies hardness at constant width. The constant-width equivalence (Q-30ff0b05e0) remains open and needs a hypothesis at least as strong as the log-width one. label: S0001
statement: Lemma (ring-buffer append cost). Let B>=1 and let a deterministic streaming machine receive blocks b_t in {0,1}^{r_t}, with total stored prefix length at most B bits. A state consisting of a B-cell circular array, a write pointer j in {0,...,B-1}, and occupied length q can incorporate a block of r bits, provided q+r<=B, by writing exactly r array cells and updating j and q. In a bit-operation model with binary pointers, this update uses O((r+1) log B) bit operations and O(B+log B) state bits; it does not require shifting the previously stored prefix. Proof: write each incoming bit to the next cell modulo B. Each binary pointer advancement and final pointer/length update costs O(log B) bit operations, so r writes and the metadata updates cost O((r+1) log B). In a word-RAM with word size ceil(log2 B), the update takes O(r+1) word operations. This proves that buffering can remove dependence on the existing prefix length from the append operation, but says nothing about the cost of later ordered decoding or oracle queries.

label: S0002
statement: statement: Lemma (ordered read from a circular prefix). Let B>=1 and let A[0..B-1] be a circular array containing q bits, 0<=q<=B, written consecutively from start position a, with next-write position j=(a+q) mod B. Assume none of these q cells has been overwritten. For every k with 0<=k<=q, the first k bits of the stored sequence can be output in order using O(k+1) word-RAM operations and O(1) words of auxiliary storage, with word size ceil(log2(B+1)). Proof: Set the read cursor c=a=(j-q) mod B. For i=0,...,k-1, output A[c] and replace c by (c+1) mod B. Inductively, before iteration i, c=(a+i) mod B. Since i<k<=q and the q stored positions are consecutive cyclic positions from a, A[c] is the (i+1)st stored bit. Thus the outputs are exactly the first k bits in order. Each iteration performs one read, one output, and one modular cursor advance, each using O(1) word-RAM operations; initialization and the k=0 case also take O(1). The cursor uses O(1) words. This establishes an ordered-read procedure for an unoverwritten circular prefix; it gives no bound on later computation or oracle-query cost.

label: S0003
statement: Lemma (trajectory invariance under time-dependent state recoding). Let a deterministic streaming computation have state sets X_t, initial state x_0, transition maps F_t:X_t×Σ→X_{t+1}, and terminal decoder D:X_T→{0,1}. For each t let π_t:X_t→Y_t be a bijection. Define recoded transitions F'_t(y,a)=π_{t+1}(F_t(π_t^{-1}(y),a)) and decoder D'(y)=D(π_T^{-1}(y)); set y_0=π_0(x_0). Then for every input stream a_0,…,a_{T−1}, the recoded computation has y_t=π_t(x_t) at every time t and returns the same output. Proof: At t=0 this is the definition of y_0. If y_t=π_t(x_t), then F'_t(y_t,a_t)=π_{t+1}(F_t(π_t^{-1}(π_t(x_t)),a_t))=π_{t+1}(F_t(x_t,a_t))=π_{t+1}(x_{t+1}); induction proves the state identity through T. Therefore D'(y_T)=D(π_T^{-1}(π_T(x_T)))=D(x_T). The lemma concerns semantic invariance only: it does not imply that π_t, π_t^{-1}, or F'_t have comparable descriptions or evaluation costs.

label: S0004
statement: statement: Lemma (continuation-distinguishable prefixes require distinct states). Let M be a deterministic one-pass machine for a language L over alphabet Σ, with a fixed initial state, deterministic transition maps, and a terminal decoder. Let P be any finite set of input prefixes such that for every distinct u,v in P there exists a suffix z_{u,v} with exactly one of uz_{u,v}, vz_{u,v} in L. Then the states reached after prefixes in P are pairwise distinct, so M has at least |P| reachable states and requires at least ceil(log2 |P|) bits to encode them. Proof: if distinct u,v reached the same state, processing their common suffix z_{u,v} would follow the same deterministic transitions and produce the same decoded answer. This contradicts that exactly one concatenation is in L. Thus the states are pairwise distinct, and encoding |P| states requires at least ceil(log2 |P|) bits. Scope: this gives a state-space lower bound for a chosen family of distinguishable prefixes, but no per-update time lower bound, including for search-MCSP.

label: S0005
statement: statement: Lemma (minimal deterministic streaming state count via residuals). Let L be any language over alphabet Σ. For each prefix u define its residual R_u={z∈Σ*: uz∈L}. In any deterministic one-pass recognizer for L, prefixes with distinct residuals reach distinct states. Conversely, if L has exactly r distinct residuals among all prefixes, a recognizer with r states exists: its states are residuals, its transition on symbol a maps R_u to R_{ua}, which is well-defined because R_u=R_v implies R_{ua}=R_{va}, and its decoder accepts R_u iff ε∈R_u. Thus the minimum number of states is exactly r (or infinite if infinitely many residuals). Proof: the first direction follows by choosing z in the symmetric difference of R_u,R_v; equal machine states would give equal outputs after z. For the converse, the transition is well-defined since z∈R_{ua} iff az∈R_u, and the decoder is well-defined by ε membership. This characterizes state complexity exactly but gives no update-time lower bound.

statement: Lemma (oracle-control obstruction). Fix a search-MCSP^A[s] streaming model and a cost measure u(M) equal to the worst-case number of updates, with oracle work charged exactly as in that model. Suppose M0 is a correct uniform one-pass algorithm in this model and u(M0) <= s^c for some constant c on all sufficiently large input parameters. Then no property P of update maps can both (i) hold for every correct uniform algorithm in this model and (ii) imply u(M)=s^{omega(1)} for every algorithm satisfying P. Proof: By (i), P holds for M0. By (ii), u(M0)=s^{omega(1)}, contradicting u(M0)<=s^c, since s^{omega(1)} eventually exceeds s^{c+1}. Thus at least one premise fails. If the cited MMW PH-oracle algorithm is correct and has polynomial update count in the exact same model and cost measure, no property shared by every correct algorithm there can prove a superpolynomial update lower bound. This says nothing about restricted models that exclude M0, or about P versus NP.

statement: Lemma (per-update control obstruction). Fix a streaming model and a cost convention, and let tau(M) be the supremum, over all updates of M on all valid streams, of the cost charged for that single update. Suppose M0 is a correct uniform algorithm in this exact model and tau(M0) <= s^c for some constant c for all sufficiently large s. Then there is no property P of update maps such that (i) every correct uniform algorithm in the model satisfies P and (ii) every algorithm satisfying P has tau(M)=s^{omega(1)}. Proof: By (i), M0 satisfies P. By (ii), tau(M0)=s^{omega(1)}, contradicting tau(M0)<=s^c. Hence at least one premise must fail. In particular, if MMW's algorithm is correct in the exact O* model and has polynomial worst-case per-update cost under its charging convention, no property shared by all correct algorithms in that model can imply a superpolynomial per-update lower bound. This lemma is conditional on that model match and implies nothing about P versus NP.

statement: statement: Lemma (residual distinguishability does not imply update cost). For every n>=1, the length-n parity language L_n={x in {0,1}^n: sum_i x_i is 1 mod 2} has 2^n pairwise continuation-distinguishable prefixes of length n, yet has a deterministic one-pass algorithm using one state bit and one XOR gate per input bit. Proof: for distinct length-n prefixes u,v, their parities differ for some pair only if the prefixes have distinct parity; hence this family itself gives at most two residual classes, so it does not establish the asserted 2^n distinguishable prefixes. Corrected statement: there are exactly two residual classes among all prefixes of L_n when considering the remaining fixed-length suffix positions, and the one-bit machine updates its parity by q <- q XOR b. Thus even a nontrivial state distinction (two residuals) is compatible with constant update cost. This rules out only an inference from residual count alone to a growing update lower bound; it says nothing about search-MCSP.

statement: statement: Unique-witness selector lemma. Let R be a relation on inputs x and b-bit strings w, and suppose the prefix-extension predicate E(x,p) = 1 iff there exists w in {0,1}^b extending p with R(x,w) holds is decidable by a deterministic algorithm in time T. If for a given x there is exactly one w with R(x,w), that witness can be found using at most b calls to E and O(b) additional work. At prefix p, query E(x,p0); append 0 if the answer is 1, and otherwise append 1. Proof: initially the empty prefix has an extension by existence. Inductively, the maintained prefix p has an extension w*. If E(x,p0)=1, choosing p0 retains an extension. Otherwise no extension starts with 0, so w* starts with 1 and p1 retains it. After b steps the prefix has length b, so its only extension is itself and R(x,p) holds. Uniqueness identifies it as the unique witness. Thus uniqueness removes any need to choose among multiple completed witnesses, but does not provide an algorithm for E; a resource improvement still requires a bound for prefix extendibility.

label: S0002
statement: statement: Lexicographic selector lemma. Let R(x,w) be any relation with witnesses w in {0,1}^b, and suppose at least one witness exists for a fixed x. Define E(x,p)=1 exactly when some R-witness extends prefix p. The lexicographically least R-witness can be found using at most b queries to E and O(b) additional bit operations. Start with the empty prefix p. At each position query E(x,p0); append 0 if it is 1, and append 1 otherwise. Proof: Inductively, p has at least one witness extension. If E(x,p0)=1, every witness extending p0 precedes every witness extending p1, so the least witness extending p also extends p0. If E(x,p0)=0, all witness extensions of p extend p1, so the least one does too. Thus after each query p remains a prefix of the lexicographically least witness. After b queries p has length b and equals that witness. Consequently, if E is decidable in time T per query, canonical witness search takes at most bT+O(b) time, excluding the cost of supplying x and any cost not included in E. This gives a precise search-to-extension reduction but alone gives no bound on E for canonical Search-MCSP witnesses.

statement: Depth-leaf bound (restricted, shrinks G0001). Let C be a fan-in-2 DAG over inputs x_1..x_n with s gates and depth d (inputs have depth 0). Its full unfolding, the tree obtained by duplicating every shared node, is a formula F_C computing the same function, and F_C has at most 2^d leaves. Scope: this is the only fixed-q case proved here; it covers depth O(log s) only and does NOT close G0001, since MMW-derived families have depth poly(s).

label: S0004
statement: Restricted fan-out bound (shrinks G0001, does not close it). Let C be a fan-in-2 Boolean DAG with n inputs and s gates, every node of out-degree at most 2, every non-root node of out-degree at least 1, and let r be the number of nodes of out-degree exactly 2. Then the full unfolding F_C computes the same Boolean function as C and has size at most (n+s)*2^r. Corollary: if r <= c*log2(s) then |F_C| <= (n+s)*s^c. PROOF: For a node u let P(u) be the set of directed paths from u to the root. The unfolding has exactly |P(u)| copies of u, so |F_C| = sum_u |P(u)| <= (n+s)*max_u |P(u)|. Let R be the set of out-degree-2 nodes, |R| = r. For p in P(u) define sigma_p in {0,1}^R: for v in R on p, sigma_p(v) is the index of the out-edge that p uses at v; for v in R not on p, sigma_p(v) = 0. Following any vector sigma from u is deterministic (out-degree-1 nodes have one edge; out-degree-2 nodes take sigma(v)), and it reaches the root because the DAG is finite and only the root has out-degree 0. The walk along sigma_p from u equals p, since at each node of p it takes p's edge. So sigma_p = sigma_q implies p = q, hence p -> sigma_p is injective into {0,1}^R and |P(u)| <= 2^r. Unfolding copies each gate with the same inputs, so F_C computes the same function. Multi-edges are handled by indexing the two edges of a gate. QED. SCOPE: DAGs with fan-out <= 2 only; the bound is linear-in-s size only when r = O(log s). It does not bound fan-out-2 chains (r = s). Nothing here is known for the MMW-derived families unless their r is shown to be O(log s). Note: the statement is the standard path-count bound (paths <= product of out-degrees at branching nodes), so its novelty is only the restriction it is used for, not the technique.

statement:
statement: Leaf count of the Lemma 3.1 top tree (bookkeeping model). Let k >= 2 be fixed, s = s(n) with n <= s and log s = o(n), l = s^k, lg = ceil(log2 s), d = floor(l/(100 s lg)) with d >= 2, D = ceil(n / log2 l). Then n(k-1)/k - n(log log s + 9)/(k log s) <= log2(d^D) <= n(k-1)/k + (k-1) log s. Hence log2(d^D) = (1 - 1/k) n + o(n); for k = 2 (the regime l >= s^2 of MMW19 Lemma 3.1) the leaf count is 2^(n/2 + o(n)), not 2^n.
derivation: (1) d >= 2 and floor loses at most a factor 2, so d >= l/(200 s lg), i.e. log d >= (k-1) log s - log lg - 8 >= (k-1) log s - log log s - 9 using lg <= 2 log s. (2) d <= l/(100 s lg) <= s^(k-1), so log d <= (k-1) log s. (3) D = ceil(n/(k log s)) lies in [n/(k log s), n/(k log s) + 1]. (4) Multiply: log(d^D) = D log d is bounded below by (n/(k log s)) times the lower bound of log d (positive by assumption) and above by (n/(k log s) + 1)(k-1) log s. Both bounds follow. (5) log s = o(n) and log log s / log s -> 0 give the (1-1/k) n + o(n) form. Scope: pure arithmetic of the d-ary top-tree bookkeeping with l = s^k; it says nothing about the oracle gates' internal formula size (open, Q-4c10cf8a13 (a)), nor about general DAG simulation G0001. It does NOT close G0001 and is not a P vs NP step. Check: experiment cm-d349c1af4a9f4d40 (EXPLORATORY, l = s^2, n = 64..16384, three s-regimes): log2 leaves/n = 0.30-0.45 and rising, inside the proved bounds at every row (e.g. n=16384, s=2^128: lower bound 7168 <= observed 7318.8 <= upper 8320).

statement:
statement: For every affine map F(x)=Ax+b on F_2^d, with augmented matrix M=[[A,b],[0,1]], any certificate consisting of r>=1, coefficients a_0,...,a_{r-1} in F_2, and the matrix identity M^r=sum_{i<r}a_i M^i certifies that every trajectory z_t=(F^t(x_0),1) satisfies z_{t+r}=sum_{i<r}a_i z_{t+i} for all t>=0. The initial states z_0,...,z_{r-1} then determine the full trajectory.
proof: By the certified identity, multiply both sides on the right by M^t z_0 to obtain M^{t+r}z_0=sum_{i<r}a_i M^{t+i}z_0 for every t>=0. Since z_j=M^jz_0, this is the claimed recurrence. Induction on t shows that the initial r states and coefficients uniquely determine all later states. This formulation does not claim every supplied witness is valid: the matrix identity must be checked. For dense (d+1)-square M, direct verification by matrix powering and matrix addition takes polynomial time in d and r; this is not the earlier O(rd^2) trajectory-only check.

structure.gap: The affine toy certificate is now sound when the full matrix annihilation identity is included. The open COMPRESS-G obligation is to obtain a sublinear-in-T fingerprint and locally checkable update rule for a concrete hierarchy-hard computation, with specified generation, verification, and decoding costs; transfer remains open.

label: S0002
statement:
statement: For every d>=0, A in F_2^{d×d}, b,x_0 in F_2^d, set M=[[A,b],[0,1]] and z_t=M^t(x_0,1). There are coefficients a_0,...,a_d in F_2 computable in time polynomial in d such that for every t>=0, z_{t+d+1}=sum_{i=0}^d a_i z_{t+i}. Proof: write the characteristic polynomial as det(XI−M)=X^{d+1}+sum_{i=0}^d a_i X^i (minus equals plus in F_2). The coefficients are computable by determinant computation over F_2. The Cayley–Hamilton theorem gives M^{d+1}+sum_i a_i M^i=0, equivalently M^{d+1}=sum_i a_i M^i. Multiplying by M^t z_0 gives the recurrence. Thus the certificate consisting of the coefficients and initial vectors z_0,...,z_d has O(d^2) bits, is constructible in polynomial time, and supports recurrence-based generation of each next state using O(d^2) bit operations. It does not give sublinear-in-T total decoding time for T states.
proof: Included in the statement; argument uses Cayley–Hamilton over F_2 and multiplication by M^t z_0.

statement: For every d>=0, A in F_2^{dxd}, b,x_0 in F_2^d, M=[[A,b],[0,1]], and integer t>=0, z_t=M^t(x_0,1) can be computed exactly using O(d^3 log(t+2)) field operations and O(d^2+log(t+1)) stored bits, without generating z_1,...,z_{t-1}. Proof: initialize R=I_{d+1}, B=M, e=t. While e>0, if e is odd replace R by RB; replace B by B^2; replace e by floor(e/2). The loop invariant R B^e=M^t holds, so at termination R=M^t. Multiply R by (x_0,1). There are O(log(t+2)) iterations, each using O((d+1)^3) field operations. The stored inputs and matrices use O(d^2+log(t+1)) bits. This is exact including t=0. It gives random access to one state, not sublinear-time output of all T states and not a hierarchy-hard fingerprint.

statement: statement: Let d,q>=0, let F(x)=Ax+b be an affine map on F_2^d, and let t_1,...,t_q be nonnegative integers given in binary. There is an exact algorithm that outputs F^{t_j}(x_0) for every j using O(q d^3 log(T+2)) field operations, where T=max_j t_j (take T=0 when q=0), and O(d^2+log(T+1)+q d) working and output bits, without generating any states at unrequested times. Proof: form the augmented matrix M=[[A,b],[0,1]]. For each t_j, compute M^{t_j} by binary exponentiation: initialize R=I and B=M, and process the binary digits of t_j, multiplying R by B for each set bit and squaring B between digits. The loop invariant is R B^e=M^{t_j} for the unprocessed exponent e; hence after the last digit R=M^{t_j}. Multiplication by (x_0,1) yields (F^{t_j}(x_0),1). Each exponent uses at most O(log(T+2)) matrix multiplications of dimension d+1, each costing O(d^3) field operations. Process queries sequentially, reusing the matrix workspace; store the input matrices and vectors, one exponent/workspace, and q output vectors, giving the stated space bound. The algorithm is exact, including t_j=0. This gives a sparse-query decoding guarantee in the affine toy model only; it does not supply a sublinear-time algorithm for emitting all T states or a certificate for a hierarchy-hard computation, so it shrinks but does not close G0001. Circumvention tests: reversible computing—no lower-bound inference; Strassen—not an operation lower bound; Barrington—not used to infer hardness; catalytic space—not used; mass production—queries are processed independently and no amortized lower bound is claimed.

statement: Lemma (single-cut rank bound, B_2). statement: Lemma L1 (repairs S0001). Let C be any circuit with arbitrary gate functions of arbitrary fan-in, nodes 0..N-1 = input variables and gates in topological order, output node f. Let A be a set of variables with complement B. Call a node u A-only if its syntactic support supp(u) (the input variables reaching u) is contained in A. Let W = {edges (u,v): u A-only, v not A-only} and kappa = |W|. Then rank_Q M_A(f) <= 2^kappa, so log2 rank <= kappa. Proof: A-only nodes compute functions of a alone, so the wire vector w(a) in {0,1}^W is a function of a. By induction in topological order, every non-A-only node has value H_v(w(a), b): its input is either A-only (the edge lies in W, value is a coordinate of w), non-A-only (induction), or a B-variable (value b_j). statement: For fixed constants k>0 and alpha>0 with alpha*k<1, suppose a deterministic uniform reduction R maps every length-T input x of L to a SAT instance phi_x of length N(T)=T^{alpha+o(1)}, runs in time o(T/log T), and has decoding and all other simulation overhead o(T/log T). If SAT is decidable in O(N^k), then L is decidable in o(T/log T). Proof: compute R(x), run the SAT algorithm on phi_x, and decode the answer. The total time is o(T/log T)+O((T^{alpha+o(1)})^k)=o(T/log T)+T^{alpha*k+o(1)}. Since alpha*k<1, choose epsilon>0 with alpha*k+epsilon<1; eventually the SAT term is at most T^{alpha*k+epsilon}=o(T/log T), because T^{1-alpha*k-epsilon}/log T tends to infinity. The sum is therefore o(T/log T), contradicting L in DTIME(T)\DTIME(o(T/log T)). At alpha*k=1 this conclusion does not follow: a T^{1+o(1)} upper bound need not be o(T/log T), and even an O(T) SAT-call bound is too large. For a fixed k, a fixed alpha<1/k is admissible only if the corresponding R_alpha is uniformly constructible with all selection, construction, auxiliary-variable, certificate, decoding, and simulation costs covered by the assumed reduction/overhead bounds. Merely having a family indexed by alpha does not handle a nonuniform or unknown choice of k.

statement: Let T tend to infinity, let alpha,k>0 be fixed with alpha*k=1, and let N(T)=T^alpha exactly. Suppose a deterministic SAT algorithm runs in O(N^k/(log N)^q) for a fixed real q. Its call time is O(T/(log T)^q), since N^k=T and log N=alpha log T. Therefore the SAT call is o(T/log T) when q>1. For q=1, this upper bound is only O(T/log T), which does not imply little-o; for q<1, it is not o(T/log T). If the reduction, decoding, and every other simulation overhead together take o(T/log T), then the full simulation takes o(T/log T) when q>1. Proof: divide the SAT call bound by T/log T to obtain O((log T)^(1-q)); this tends to zero exactly when q>1. Adding the assumed little-o overhead preserves little-o. This lemma is only for exact N=T^alpha; it does not assert the same boundary for N=T^(alpha+o(1)).

statement: Let alpha,k>0 be fixed with alpha*k=1, let q be any fixed real, and let g(T)>0 satisfy log g(T)=o(log T). Define the benchmark B(T)=N(T)^k/(log N(T))^q for N(T)=T^alpha*g(T), for sufficiently large T. Then B(T)=o(T/log T) if and only if g(T)^k/(log T)^(q-1) tends to zero as T tends to infinity. statement: L-GF3: For a positive 1-in-3 CNF F on variables 0..n-1 (3 distinct variables per clause) with incidence matrix A over GF(3) and V = {x in F_3^n : Ax = 1 mod 3}: (1) F is satisfiable iff V contains a 0/1 point; (2) if V is nonempty then |V| = 3^(n - rank_3 A), and if V is empty then F is unsatisfiable; (3) hence #SAT(F) <= 3^(n - rank_3 A). Proof: (1) a 1-in-3 solution gives clause sums exactly 1, so Ax = 1 mod 3; conversely a 0/1 point with every clause sum = 1 mod 3 has clause sums in {0,1,2,3} congruent to 1, hence equal to 1. (2) Gaussian elimination over F_3 on [A|1] gives V = x0 + ker A, dim ker A = n - rank_3 A. (3) follows from (1) and (2). Scope: restates S0001 (same claim, same scope). Not a speed-up: it beats 2^n only when rank_3 A > (1 - log_3 2) n, about 0.369 n. Finite check cm-40b8f023cf164326 (360 instances, n=6..9) matches the claim but is not a proof.

statement: PROOF. Distinct rows of M are 0/1 vectors in V, so they lie in V and the bound is |V ∩ {0,1}^n| <= 2^r. Let B be an r x n matrix whose rows are a basis of V. B has rank r, so it has r linearly independent columns; let S be their index set, |S| = r. For v = cB in V (c in Q^r), v_S = c B_S, and B_S is invertible, so c is determined by v_S and hence v is determined by v_S. So the restriction x -> x_S is injective on V. It maps V ∩ {0,1}^n into {0,1}^S, which has 2^r elements. Hence |V ∩ {0,1}^n| <= 2^r. For the corollary: fix an order pi that attains W_rank. Every cut k has distinct-row count <= 2^{rank_k} <= 2^{W_rank}, so the max over cuts is <= 2^{W_rank}; minimising over orders gives W_OBDD <= 2^{W_rank}. Check: F={x0+x1+x2=1} has W_rank=2, W_OBDD=3 <= 4. The lemma is elementary and is probably standard in the rank-versus-OBDD literature; it is recorded as a verified finite-scope step, not as new. label: S0023
statement: LEMMA (rank sandwich for OBDD width). Let f:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, let pi be a variable order, and for 1<=l<=n-1 let M_l(f,pi) be the 0/1 matrix with rows indexed by assignments a to the first l variables, columns by assignments b to the remaining variables, entries f(a,b). Let R_l = rank over GF(2) of M_l, and D_l = number of DISTINCT rows of M_l (= number of distinct subfunctions f|_a). Then R_l <= D_l <= 2^{R_l}. Consequently minRank(f) <= min_pi max_l D_l(f,pi) <= 2^{minRank(f)}, where minRank(f) = min_pi max_l R_l(f,pi). PROOF. Let V be the GF(2) row space of M_l, dim V = R_l, so |V| = 2^{R_l}. Every row lies in V, and the rows span V by definition, so the set of distinct rows is a spanning set of V; hence D_l >= R_l. Also the distinct rows are elements of V, so D_l <= |V| = 2^{R_l}. For the consequence: for each pi, max_l R_l <= max_l D_l, so minRank <= min_pi max_l D_l. For pi* attaining minRank, max_l D_l(f,pi*) <= 2^{max_l R_l(f,pi*)} = 2^{minRank}, so min_pi max_l D_l <= 2^{minRank}. Each step is elementary linear algebra over GF(2); no computation is used. SCOPE: all Boolean f, all n>=2, all orders. STATUS OF THE GAP: this sandwich is two-sided but does not decide G0001. The lower side is trivial (D >= R). The upper side gives only the exponential relation, not the reverse direction that G0001 asks for. It is not a P vs NP claim and carries no barrier content (no lower bound is proved).

label: S0026
statement: Proof: an assignment x falsifies C_i for all i in S iff, for each literal l in C_i, x makes l false; so the set of such x is {x : x agrees with the forced values of S}. If the forced values conflict, the set is empty; if consistent, it is a subcube fixing exactly |V(S)| variables, of size 2^(n-|V(S)|). Inclusion-exclusion over the falsified-clause events A_i = {x falsifies C_i} gives #(no A_i) = sum_S (-1)^|S| |intersection_{i in S} A_i|, which is the formula. Clauses with complementary literals are never falsified and are handled by the conflict case. Status: CLAIMED, the argument is elementary and standard; the value is a precise statement, not new mathematics. The sum has 2^m terms, so it gives no polynomial-time algorithm.

structure.lemma: S-54f648a904 (formal). Let F = C_1 AND ... AND C_m be a CNF on variables 0..n-1, each clause a set of literals. For S subset of {1..m} let V(S) be the set of variables occurring in clauses of S, and say S is consistent if the assignments that falsify every literal of every clause in S exist, i.e. no variable is required both 0 and 1. Then #F = sum_{S} (-1)^|S| N(S), with N(S) = 2^(n - |V(S)|) if S is consistent and N(S) = 0 otherwise.

statement: S-AND-WIDTH-01: Let F, G: {0,1}^k -> {0,1} be Boolean functions on the same prefix-cut, with residual functions f_a = F(a, .) and g_a = G(a, .) over the suffix variables, and D(H) = number of distinct residual functions of H over prefixes a. Then D(F AND G) <= D(F) D(G). If in addition the zero residual occurs among the residuals of both F and G, then D(F AND G) <= 1 + (D(F)-1)(D(G)-1). Proof: the residual of F AND G at a is f_a AND g_a, so D(F AND G) is at most the number of distinct pairs (f_a, g_a), giving the product bound. For the sharpened bound, a nonzero residual f_a AND g_a forces f_a and g_a nonzero, so the nonzero residuals of F AND G lie in {u AND v : u in N_F, v in N_G}, where N_F is the set of nonzero residuals of F, and |N_F| = D(F)-1 when zero is a residual of F (likewise G). This gives at most (D(F)-1)(D(G)-1) nonzero residuals plus one zero residual. Scope: finite Boolean functions with a fixed variable cut; this is a width bound for pointwise AND of residual sets, not a bound on any algorithm's running time.

Proof: the residual of F AND G at a is f_a AND g_a, so D(F AND G) is at most the number of distinct pairs (f_a, g_a), giving the product bound. For the sharpened bound, a nonzero residual f_a AND g_a forces f_a and g_a nonzero, so the nonzero residuals of F AND G lie in {u AND v : u in N_F, v in N_G}, where N_F is the set of nonzero residuals of F, and |N_F| = D(F)-1 when zero is a residual of F (likewise G). This gives at most (D(F)-1)(D(G)-1) nonzero residuals plus one zero residual. Scope: finite Boolean functions with a fixed variable cut; this is a width bound for pointwise AND of residual sets, not a bound on any algorithm's running time.

label: S0042
statement: S-sandwich-rank-OBDD (LEMMA, CLAIMED). Scope: any Boolean f on {0,1}^n, any variable order, any cut k. Let M_k be the 2^k x 2^(n-k) matrix M_k[a,b] = f(a,b) with prefix a and suffix b. Let D_k = number of distinct rows of M_k and R_k = rank over Q of M_k. Claim: R_k <= D_k <= 2^(R_k). Proof. (i) The D_k distinct rows span the row space of M_k, which contains all rows, so R_k <= D_k. (ii) Let V be the row space of M_k, dim V = R_k. Choose R_k columns S on which the projection x -> x_S is injective on V (a basis matrix of V has R_k independent columns). The distinct rows are distinct elements of V in {0,1}^(2^(n-k)), so their restrictions to S are pairwise distinct and lie in {0,1}^S, which has 2^(R_k) elements. Hence D_k <= 2^(R_k). Consequence: write W_rank(pi) = max_k R_k and W_OBDD(pi) = max_k D_k. For every order pi, W_rank(pi) <= W_OBDD(pi) <= 2^(W_rank(pi)); minimising over pi gives min_pi W_rank <= min_pi W_OBDD <= 2^(min_pi W_rank). Gap relation: G0001 asks whether min_pi W_OBDD <= poly(min_pi W_rank). The sandwich reduces G0001 to whether the factor 2^(W_rank) can be replaced by a polynomial in the minimum-over-orders setting; it does not close G0001. Per-cut tightness: the MUX cut of S0007 has D = 2^R, so no per-order polynomial improvement exists; only the minimum over orders can help. Barrier label (diagnostic): not applicable, no complexity lower bound is claimed. Review status: CLAIMED; this session cannot review its own step.
