label: S0043
statement:
statement: For every n >= 2, every order of the n variables and every cut with prefix set A (|A| = k): rank_Q(M_A) <= (k+1)(n-k+1) <= floor((n+2)^2/4), where M_A is the cut matrix of HWB_n(x) = x_{|x|} (0 if |x| = 0) with rows indexed by prefix assignments a and columns by suffix assignments b.
proof: Split rows of M_A by the weight s in {0..k} of a and columns by the weight t in {0..n-k} of b. This gives (k+1)(n-k+1) blocks R_{s,t}, and M_A is the sum of their zero-padded versions. On R_{s,t}, |a union b| = s+t = j is constant, so the entry equals x_j for a fixed variable j. If j = 0 the block is zero. If j in A, the entry is a_j, which depends only on the row, so the block has rank <= 1. If j in B, the entry is b_j, which depends only on the column, so the block has rank <= 1. Rank is subadditive, so rank_Q(M_A) <= (k+1)(n-k+1). Maximising over k gives floor((n+2)^2/4).
shrinks: G0001 rank side for HWB_n: W_rank(HWB_n) <= floor((n+2)^2/4) for every order. Does not supply the superpolynomial min-over-orders OBDD width lower bound.

label: S0044
statement:
statement: Let M be a matrix over Q with k columns and r = rank_Q(M). The number of distinct 0/1 rows of M is at most 2^r. Consequently, for a fixed variable order, the number of distinct residual functions at a cut is at most 2^{rank_Q(M_cut)}. Scope: fixed order only; min over orders is NOT covered (G0001 stays open).
proof: Let V = rowspace(M), dim V = r. Choose r columns J with a nonzero r x r minor. The projection pi_J: V -> Q^J has image of dimension rank(M restricted to J) = r, so it is injective on V. Each distinct 0/1 row lies in V and maps injectively into {0,1}^J, which has 2^r elements. The GF(2) inequality rank_GF2(M) <= rank_Q(M) holds because a minor nonzero mod 2 is nonzero over Q.

label: S0045
statement: BUCKET-ELIM-EXACT (standard, Dechter 1999; recorded as bookkeeping, closes no obligation). Let F(x_1..x_n) = prod_{i=1..k} f_i(x_{S_i}) with f_i : {0,1}^{S_i} -> Z_{>=0}. Fix an order v_1..v_n. At step t, let I_t be the factors whose scope contains v_t, U_t the union of their scopes, and g_t(x_{U_t \ {v_t}}) = sum_{x_{v_t} in {0,1}} prod_{i in I_t} f_i. Then (a) the sum of F over {0,1}^n equals the value of the final scalar product obtained by the recursion (distributivity of product over sum, since v_t occurs only in the factors of I_t at step t); (b) the product table at step t has 2^{|U_t|} entries and g_t has 2^{|U_t|-1} entries; (c) so the largest table is at most 2^{w+1}, w = max_t (|U_t| - 1). Proof: (a) induction on t, using that v_t occurs in no factor outside I_t at that point; (b) by definition of U_t. Scope: finite Boolean, nonnegative weights, any fixed order. Consequence: exact counting for positive 1-in-3 CNF costs sum_t 2^{|U_t|} arithmetic operations, with the 3-variable clause table having 3 of 8 entries nonzero.

label: S0046
statement:
statement: Let M be a 0/1 matrix over Q with rank_Q(M) = r. Then M has at most 2^r distinct rows. Consequently, for a fixed variable order and cut k, the number of distinct residual functions D_k <= 2^{r_k}, where r_k = rank_Q of the cut communication matrix, and the OBDD width of that order is <= 2^{max_k r_k}.
derivation: Let V in Q^B be the row space of M, dim V = r. Choose a basis of V, form the r x |B| matrix of basis vectors, and pick r columns J on which it is invertible. The projection pi_J: V -> Q^J is then injective. Every row of M lies in V and has entries in {0,1}, so pi_J(row) lies in {0,1}^J, which has 2^r elements. Hence a row is determined by at most 2^r values and M has at most 2^r distinct rows. Applying this to the cut matrix of each level k gives D_k <= 2^{r_k}. Scope: this is an exponential bound 2^{O(W_rank)} only; it does not give the polynomial form poly(W_rank) asked in the gap.

label: S0047
statement:
statement: For every r >= 1 there is a 0/1 matrix M_r with rank_Q(M_r) = r and exactly 2^r distinct rows, so the bound 'distinct rows <= 2^{rank_Q}' of S0046 is tight for arbitrary 0/1 matrices.
derivation: Index rows by x in {0,1}^r and columns by j in [r], with M_r[x,j] = x_j. The rows x = e_i (unit vectors) are the standard basis of Q^r, so rank_Q(M_r) = r (at most r columns, and r independent rows). The row indexed by x equals x itself, so the rows are pairwise distinct and there are 2^r of them. Scope: arbitrary 0/1 matrices. Not claimed: that M_r is a cut matrix of any formula or THR o THR circuit of size poly(r). Consequence: closing G0001 (poly form) needs a property of cut matrices of bounded-size circuits beyond their rank.

label: S0050
statement:
statement: Let F: {0,1}^n -> {0,1} and let S be a set of variables. Let M_S be the cut matrix with rows indexed by assignments to S, columns by assignments to the complement, and entries F. Let K(S) be the number of distinct rows of M_S and R(S) the rank over Q of M_S. Then K(S) <= 2^R(S). Consequently W(F) <= 2^R(F), where W(F) is the min over variable orders of the max over prefixes of K, and R(F) is the min over orders of the max over prefixes of R.
proof: Let r = R(S) and let V be the row space of M_S over Q, so dim V = r. Choose r linearly independent columns J of M_S. Since these columns span the column space, the submatrix M_S[:,J] has rank r, so its row space has dimension r. That row space is the image of V under the projection p_J to Q^J, so p_J is injective on V. Each distinct row of M_S is a distinct 0/1 vector lying in V, so distinct rows have distinct restrictions to J, and those restrictions lie in {0,1}^J, a set of size 2^r. Hence K(S) <= 2^r. For the consequence, take an order pi minimising the max over prefixes of R. Then the max over prefixes of K is at most 2^(max R), so W(F) <= 2^R(F). Tightness: for rows x in {0,1}^r and columns j in [r], with M[x,j] = x_j, the rank is r and K = 2^r, so the bound is attained. Scope: arbitrary Boolean functions, any n. This is the multiplicative repair of H_A and is exponential, so it does not yet give a polynomial width bound.

label: S0051
statement:
statement: Let F = AND of factors f_1..f_m on Boolean variables, each factor on at most 3 variables. For a variable set S let dS be the set of variables in S that occur in a factor which also contains a variable outside S. Let K(S) be the number of distinct residual functions of F on the complement, indexed by assignments to S. Then K(S) <= 2^|dS| + 1.
proof: Split factors into I (inside S), J (crossing), O (inside complement). For prefix assignment a, the residual is g(a) AND h(b) AND over f in J of f(a restricted to S cap f, b), where g(a) = AND over I of f(a) and h(b) = AND over O of f(b) does not depend on a. Each crossing factor depends on a only through a restricted to dS. So the residual is determined by the pair (g(a), a restricted to dS). If g(a)=0 the residual is the zero function (one residual). If g(a)=1 it is determined by a restricted to dS, at most 2^|dS| residuals. Hence K(S) <= 2^|dS| + 1. Consequence: min over orders of max over prefixes of K is at most 2^vs(F) + 1, where vs is the vertex separation number of the primal graph. Scope: conjunctive formulas with bounded factor size, any n. Not new: standard pathwidth-to-OBDD fact. Does not give a polynomial width for random 1-in-3 formulas, where vs is linear in n.

label: S0093
statement: statement: For a positive 1-in-3 CNF and a fixed variable cut with b clauses meeting both sides, the number of distinct residual Boolean functions is at most 4^b+1. For each crossing clause, assigning its variables on the processed side leaves one of at most four residual conditions on the unprocessed variables (including constant true/false). The conjunction of all clauses wholly on the processed side contributes only a global zero/nonzero flag; clauses wholly on the unprocessed side are common to every residual. Hence each residual is determined by a tuple of at most b crossing-clause forms and that flag, giving at most 4^b+1 possibilities.

label: S0094
statement: statement: For the positive 1-in-3 formula F(x0,x1,x2) defined by x0+x1+x2=1 with Boolean variables, every variable order has maximum number of distinct residual rows 3 and maximum rational cut-matrix rank 2. By symmetry it suffices to inspect prefix sizes k=0,1,2,3. At k=0 the single cut row is nonzero, so the width/rank are 1/1. At k=1, the two rows indexed by x0=0 and x0=1 are (0,1,1,0) and (1,0,0,1); they are distinct and linearly independent, giving 2/2. At k=2, rows indexed by (x0,x1)=00,01,10,11 are respectively (0,1),(1,0),(1,0),(0,0), giving 3 distinct rows and rank 2. At k=3 the rows are the one-column values of F, with both 0 and 1 occurring, giving 2 distinct rows and rank 1. Thus the maxima are 3 and 2; this repairs the incorrect claim that the k=1 cut has rank 1.

label: S0095
statement: statement: Let F be a conjunction of positive EXACT1 clauses, each on three distinct Boolean variables, and fix a variable cut with b crossing clauses. The number of distinct residual Boolean functions after assignments to the processed side is at most 3^b+1. For a crossing clause with one processed variable, the residual condition is one of x+y=1, x+y=0, or false; with two processed variables it is one of x=1, x=0, or false. Thus each crossing clause contributes at most three possible residual functions. Clauses entirely on the processed side contribute a single global satisfiable/unsatisfiable flag, while clauses entirely on the unprocessed side are common to all residuals. If the flag is false the residual is the zero function; otherwise it is specified by a tuple of at most b crossing-clause forms conjoined with the common unprocessed-side formula. Hence there are at most 3^b+1 residual functions.

label: S0096
statement: statement: Let F be a conjunction of positive EXACT1 clauses, each on three distinct Boolean variables, and fix a cut of the variables into processed set X and unprocessed set Y. If exactly b clauses meet both X and Y, then F has at most 3^b+1 distinct residual Boolean functions on Y as assignments to X vary. Proof: A clause wholly in X is either satisfied or violated by an assignment to X; all such clauses together contribute one global flag. If any is violated, the residual is the zero function. Clauses wholly in Y form a fixed common conjunct. For a crossing clause, let p be its number of variables in X (p is 1 or 2), let q=3-p, and let a be the number of its X-variables assigned 1. Its residual condition on its q Y-variables is that their sum equals 1-a. For p=1, a is 0 or 1, yielding respectively a two-variable EXACT1 condition or a two-variable zero-sum condition. For p=2, a is 0, 1, or 2, yielding respectively a unary value-1 condition, a unary value-0 condition, or the identically false condition. Thus each crossing clause has at most three possible residual functions. The tuple of these forms for the b crossing clauses, together with the global flag, determines the full residual after conjoining the fixed Y-only clauses. When the flag is true there are at most 3^b such tuples; when false all assignments yield the same zero residual. Therefore the total is at most 3^b+1. In particular, for any fixed variable order whose every prefix cut has at most B crossing clauses, its OBDD width at every level is at most 3^B+1. This is a boundary-based width bound; it makes no claim relating B to rational cut rank and does not settle G0001.

structure.proved_step: statement: Let F be a conjunction of positive EXACT1 clauses, each on three distinct Boolean variables, and fix a cut of the variables into processed set X and unprocessed set Y. If exactly b clauses meet both X and Y, then F has at most 3^b+1 distinct residual Boolean functions on Y as assignments to X vary. Proof: A clause wholly in X is either satisfied or violated by an assignment to X; all such clauses together contribute one global flag. If any is violated, the residual is the zero function. label: S0098
statement: Repair of S0094: For F(x0,x1,x2)=1 iff x0+x1+x2=1 on Boolean variables, every variable order has maximum residual-row count 3 and maximum rational cut-matrix rank 2. Proof: F is symmetric, so every order is equivalent under a variable permutation. For the cut after zero variables there is one nonzero row, hence count 1 and rank 1. After one variable, using remaining assignments 00,01,10,11 as columns, the rows for the processed bit 0 and 1 are respectively (0,1,1,0) and (1,0,0,0). They are distinct and linearly independent over Q, so count 2 and rank 2. After two variables, rows for processed assignments 00,01,10,11 over the final bit are (0,1),(1,0),(1,0),(0,0); hence there are 3 distinct rows and rank 2. After all variables the one-column rows are the attained values 0 and 1, giving count 2 and rank 1. Taking maxima gives 3 and 2. This repairs the erroneous k=1 truth-table entry; it establishes only this three-variable example and does not address the asymptotic gap.

label: S0099
statement: statement: For every finite Boolean matrix M over Q of rank r, the number of distinct rows of M is at most 2^r. Proof: Let V be the rational row space of M, with dimension r. Choose r coordinate positions J such that coordinate projection V -> Q^J is injective, by taking pivot coordinates of a basis matrix of V. This projection is also injective on V intersect {0,1}^m. Its image lies in {0,1}^J, which has 2^r elements. Every distinct row of M belongs to that intersection, so there are at most 2^r distinct rows. If r=0, V={0}, and the conclusion still holds.

statement:
statement_start: For every positive EXACT1 CNF F whose clauses use three distinct Boolean variables, and every cut X|Y crossed by b clauses, the number of distinct residual Boolean functions on Y induced by assignments to X is at most 3^b+1.
proof: For an assignment to X, its residual is the conjunction of the fixed Y-only clauses, the residual conditions from crossing clauses, and a flag for whether all X-only clauses are satisfied. A crossing clause with one X-variable leaves either a two-variable exact-one or zero-sum condition, so has at most two forms. With two X-variables, their sum is 0, 1, or 2, leaving a unary value-1 condition, a unary value-0 condition, or false, so has at most three forms. Thus the b crossing clauses have at most 3^b tuples of residual forms. If the X-only flag is false, the residual is the zero function; otherwise the tuple determines the residual after conjunction with the common Y-only clauses. There are at most 3^b+1 residual functions. Therefore, for any variable order with at most B crossing clauses at every prefix, OBDD width at each level is at most 3^B+1.

statement:
statement: For every positive EXACT1-3 CNF F and every partition of its variables into L and R, if b clauses intersect both sides, the number of distinct residual Boolean functions F|_x on R induced by assignments x to L is at most 2^b+1.
proof: For each assignment x to L, first test every clause wholly contained in L; if one fails, F|_x is the identically false function. For every crossing clause C, record t_C(x), the number of its variables in L assigned 1. If t_C(x)>=2, then the exact-one constraint cannot be satisfied for any assignment on R, so again F|_x is identically false. Otherwise every t_C lies in {0,1}. The value of F on an assignment y to R is the conjunction of all clauses wholly in R and, for each crossing clause C, the condition sum_{v in C intersect R} y_v = 1-t_C(x). Thus for two left assignments passing the checks with the same vector (t_C) over the b crossing clauses, their residual functions agree on every y. There are at most 2^b such vectors and at most one additional false residual, giving the bound.
scope: All finite positive exact-one 3-CNF formulas, arbitrary variable cuts; b is the number of clauses meeting both sides. This is a general proved-step candidate, not a P vs NP result.

label: S0106
statement: statement: Cut-factorization rank bound for tensor networks. Let G be a finite graph partitioned into vertex sets A and B. Each edge e has an index set [d_e], d_e positive, and each vertex carries an arbitrary rational tensor indexed by its incident edges and an optional finite external input x_v. Let F(x_A,x_B) be the scalar from summing the product of vertex tensors over all edge indices. If C is the set of edges crossing the partition and D=product_{e in C} d_e (empty product 1), then the rational rank of M[x_A,x_B]=F(x_A,x_B) is at most D. Proof: For each assignment z to the indices on C, contract all tensors and summed indices internal to A while fixing C to z, obtaining u_z(x_A); contract the B side analogously to obtain v_z(x_B). Regrouping the finite contraction by z gives F(x_A,x_B)=sum_z u_z(x_A)v_z(x_B). Thus M is a sum of D outer products, each of rank at most one, so rank_Q(M)<=D. This allows arbitrary rational entries, signs, cancellation, and finite external-input domains. It bounds a specified vertex cut only; it asserts nothing about optimal contraction orders, bit complexity, or the min-over-orders OBDD/rank gap.

statement:
statement: Let F be a conjunction of positive EXACT1 clauses, each on three distinct Boolean variables. For a fixed variable cut X|Y, let b1 and b2 be the numbers of crossing clauses with respectively one and two variables in X. The number of distinct residual Boolean functions on Y induced by assignments to X is at most 2^b1*3^b2+1. Proof: a crossing clause with p variables in X leaves the condition that its Y variables sum to 1-a, where a is the number of assigned 1s in X. For p=1 there are at most two possible residual forms; for p=2 there are at most three. The Y-only clauses are a common conjunct. All X-only clauses contribute a single global flag; if false the residual is zero, and otherwise the tuple of crossing forms determines it. Thus there are at most 2^b1*3^b2 tuples and one additional zero residual. Consequently, for any fixed variable order, the OBDD width at each cut is at most 2^b1*3^b2+1.
proof: For each assignment to X, every X-only clause is either true or false. If any is false, the entire residual is the zero function. Otherwise, each crossing EXACT1 clause reduces to the condition that the sum of its Y variables equals 1 minus the number a of its X variables assigned 1. When p=1, a∈{0,1}, hence at most two forms. When p=2, a∈{0,1,2}, hence at most three forms. The conjunction of all Y-only clauses is fixed. Therefore, among assignments for which the X-only flag is true, the residual is determined by a tuple with at most 2^b1*3^b2 possibilities; assignments with false flag contribute at most one additional residual, the zero function. The OBDD consequence follows because its width at a cut equals the number of distinct residual functions there.

statement:
statement: For any Boolean function f:X×Y→{0,1}, any fixed cut X|Y, and any field K, let M be its 0/1 communication matrix over K, let r=rank_K(M), and let D be the number of distinct rows of M. Then D≤2^r. Consequently, for every variable order π, the maximum number of residual functions at a cut is at most 2^{max_cut rank_K(M_cut)}; minimizing over π gives W_OBDD(f)≤2^{W_rank,K(f)}.
proof: Let U be the row space of M, of dimension r. The coordinate functionals on K^Y restrict to a spanning set of U*, so choose coordinates y_1,...,y_r whose restrictions form a basis of U*. The map φ:U→K^r given by these coordinates is injective. Every row of M is in U and has only 0/1 entries, so its image lies in {0,1}^r. Distinct rows therefore have distinct images, proving D≤2^r. If r=0, U={0} and D≤1. At a variable-order cut, rows correspond exactly to residual functions on the unprocessed variables. Apply the bound at each cut, then minimize over orders; monotonicity of 2^x gives the stated inequality.
scope: All finite Boolean functions, fixed variable cuts and variable orders, and any field K. This comparison does not construct a family attaining an exponential gap.

label: S0121
statement: statement_start: REPAIR of S0104: Let F be a positive EXACT1 3-CNF on n variables and m clauses with three distinct variables per clause. For a fixed variable order whose every prefix cut has at most B crossing clauses, exact #SAT is computable in O((n+m) * 3^B * poly(B)) arithmetic operations. Proof: Maintain a map from residual signatures to counts. A signature comprises (1) a failure flag, and (2) for each of the at most B crossing clauses, a residual condition from the set {EXACT1 on 3 vars, EXACT1 on 2 vars (sum=1), EXACT1 on 1 var (value=1), forced-0, forced-1, false}. There are at most 7^B * 2 signatures. Initialize with the empty assignment (flag=false, all clauses in future set) with count 1. At step k (variable v = order[k]), for each signature, branch on v=0 and v=1. To update: only clauses containing v change status. For each such clause, update its residual condition in O(1) time using a precomputed transition table (7 states x 2 values). Clauses not containing v keep their condition. After updating both children, merge identical signatures by summing counts. Merging uses hashing: O(7^B * poly(B)) per level. Total work per level: O(3^B * deg(v) * poly(B) + 7^B * poly(B)) = O(3^B * deg(v) * poly(B)) since 7^B = O(3^B * poly(B))? Wait, 7^B is larger than 3^B. Actually max signatures is 2 * 7^B. But the number of *active* signatures is at most 2 * 3^B + 1 because each crossing EXACT1 clause has at most 3 residual conditions when the failure flag is false (sum=0, sum=1, or false), plus the all-false state. So active signatures <= 2 * 3^B + 1. Updating a signature takes O(deg(v)) time (only clauses containing v change). Merging takes O(3^B * poly(B)) via hashing. Sum over n levels: O(3^B * poly(B) * sum_v deg(v) + n * 3^B * poly(B)) = O(3^B * poly(B) * (3m + n)) = O((n+m) * 3^B * poly(B)). At level n, sum counts of signatures with flag=false and no crossing clauses (all satisfied). This proves the runtime bound.

label: S0122
statement: statement_start: REPAIR of S0094: For the positive 1-in-3 formula F(x0,x1,x2) defined by x0+x1+x2=1 with Boolean variables, every variable order has maximum number of distinct residual rows 3 and maximum rational cut-matrix rank 2. Proof: By symmetry it suffices to inspect the order x0,x1,x2 and prefix sizes k=0,1,2,3. At k=0 the single cut row is the full truth table (nonzero), so width=1, rank=1. At k=1, rows indexed by x0=0 and x0=1 over (x1,x2) in order 00,01,10,11: F(0,x1,x2)=EXACT1(x1,x2) gives (0,1,1,0); F(1,x1,x2)=EXACT1(1,x1,x2) gives (1,0,0,0) since 1+x1+x2=1 requires x1=x2=0. These two rows are distinct and linearly independent (a(0,1,1,0)+b(1,0,0,0)=(b,a,a,0)=0 => a=b=0), so width=2, rank=2. At k=2, rows for (x0,x1)=00,01,10,11: 00->F(0,0,x2)=x2 gives (0,1); 01->F(0,1,x2)=1-x2 gives (1,0); 10->same as 01 gives (1,0); 11->impossible gives (0,0). Three distinct rows: (0,1),(1,0),(0,0), spanning 2D space, so width=3, rank=2. At k=3, rows are the values of F, both 0 and 1 occur, width=2, rank=1. Thus maxima over all cuts are 3 distinct rows and rank 2.

label: S0126
statement: statement: For every Boolean function f and every field F, let W_rank(pi) be the maximum F-rank of a cut matrix under variable order pi, and W_OBDD(pi) the maximum number of distinct residual rows at any cut. Then min_pi W_rank(pi) <= min_pi W_OBDD(pi) <= 2^(min_pi W_rank(pi)). Proof: At a cut whose matrix has rank r, choose r pivot coordinates such that projection of its row space to those coordinates is injective. Every residual row is binary, so its projection is in {0,1}^r; hence there are at most 2^r distinct residual rows. Therefore W_OBDD(pi) <= 2^W_rank(pi) for each order pi. Since there are finitely many orders, choose pi* minimizing W_rank. Then min_pi W_OBDD(pi) <= W_OBDD(pi*) <= 2^W_rank(pi*) = 2^(min_pi W_rank(pi)). The lower bound follows since rank is at most the number of distinct rows at every cut, hence W_rank(pi) <= W_OBDD(pi) for each pi.

statement:
statement: Finite-alphabet row bound. Let F be a field, A a finite subset of F, and M an arbitrary matrix over F whose entries all lie in A. If rank_F(M)=r and D is the number of distinct rows of M, then D<=|A|^r. Proof: Choose a basis b_1,...,b_r of the row space. There are r coordinate positions j_1,...,j_r such that the r-by-r matrix (b_i[j_t]) is nonsingular: this follows because the coordinate functionals restricted to the r-dimensional row space span its dual, so a basis can be selected from them. Consequently the restriction map from the row space to these r coordinates is injective. Distinct rows therefore have distinct restrictions to j_1,...,j_r. Each restriction belongs to A^r, which has |A|^r elements, proving the bound. For a Boolean cut matrix, A={0,1}, so every cut with field rank r has at most 2^r distinct residual rows. For any fixed variable order pi, taking maxima over cuts gives W_OBDD(pi)<=2^W_rank(pi). Taking an order minimizing W_rank yields min_pi W_OBDD(pi)<=2^(min_pi W_rank(pi)); and rank<=number of distinct rows at each cut gives the reverse inequality min_pi W_rank(pi)<=min_pi W_OBDD(pi). This supplies the pivot-coordinate proof for the minimum-over-orders comparison, without relying on S0126.
proof: The coordinate functionals on an r-dimensional subspace of F^N span its dual: if their span were proper, a nonzero vector of the subspace would be annihilated by every coordinate functional, hence would be the zero vector, contradiction. Select r coordinate functionals forming a dual basis. Their joint restriction is injective. Distinct matrix rows are distinct vectors in the row space, so injectivity gives distinct coordinate tuples. Since every entry is in A, there are at most |A|^r such tuples. The Boolean cut-matrix corollary follows with A={0,1}. For the order comparison, the per-cut bounds imply W_OBDD(pi)<=2^W_rank(pi) for every pi. label: S0128
statement: For every integer k≥1, let F_k be the Boolean function on 3k variables that accepts exactly assignments having Hamming weight one on each of k disjoint triples. In the variable order that processes each triple consecutively, every cut has at most three distinct residual rows and rational cut-matrix rank at most two, and both maxima are attained. Proof: At a cut between triples, any prefix violating a completed constraint gives the zero residual; every other prefix gives the same nonzero suffix function. Thus there are at most two rows and rank at most one. At a cut inside a triple, completed triples again yield either zero or a common factor 1. If t∈{1,2} variables of the current triple have been assigned and their sum is a, its residual is the indicator that the remaining variables sum to 1−a. For a>1 it is zero. For a≤1, the only possible nonzero residuals are the indicators of two different target sums, 1 and 0. The unprocessed triples contribute a common nonzero suffix factor. Therefore there are at most two nonzero rows plus the zero row; the two nonzero rows are linearly independent over Q because their supports are disjoint and nonempty. Hence the rank is at most two. At a cut after two variables of a triple, the three residuals (indicator of the last variable being 1, indicator of it being 0, and zero), each extended by the same nonzero suffix factor, are all attained. Thus both maxima are attained.

label: S0129
statement: statement: Block-product lemma (scoped constructive special case). Let k>=1 and let f_i:{0,1}^{b_i}->{0,1} be nonzero Boolean functions on pairwise disjoint variable blocks. Define F(x^(1),...,x^(k))=product_i f_i(x^(i)), and use an order that processes the blocks consecutively, with any fixed internal order within each block. At any cut lying inside block j, each prefix induces either the zero residual, or a residual of f_j multiplied by the fixed nonzero suffix function product_{i>j} f_i; therefore the number of distinct residual rows is at most D_j+1, where D_j is the maximum number of distinct residual rows of f_j over its internal cuts. The cut matrix rank over any field is at most R_j, the maximum internal cut rank of f_j. At block boundaries the residual count is at most 2 and rank at most 1. Thus W_OBDD(F) <= max(2, 1+max_j D_j), and W_rank(F) <= max(1,max_j R_j), in this block order. Proof: A prefix either falsifies an already completed block (giving the zero row) or satisfies every completed block (whose product is 1); within the current block its continuation is exactly one residual of f_j, and the unprocessed blocks contribute the same nonzero suffix factor to every such row. Distinct nonzero residuals remain distinct after multiplication by a nonzero Boolean function, since that suffix has at least one satisfying assignment. Their span dimension is unchanged by adjoining zero and by tensoring each row with the same nonzero suffix vector, so the rank is at most R_j. At a boundary the only rows are zero and the common suffix product. This is a constructive fixed-order bound for disjoint block products; it does not settle the minimum-over-orders gap G0001.

statement: Let M be a matrix over any field whose entries all lie in {0,1}. If rank(M)=r, then M has at most 2^r distinct rows. Proof: let U be the row space of M, of dimension r. Choose r coordinate positions J such that the coordinate projection pi_J: U -> F^r is injective; such positions exist by taking pivot columns of a matrix whose rows are a basis of U. Every row of M lies in U and has entries in {0,1}. If two rows have the same projection, injectivity implies they are the same row. The image of the set of distinct rows is contained in {0,1}^r, a set of cardinality 2^r, proving the bound. This is a per-cut statement for Boolean communication matrices and makes no claim about a minimum-over-orders separation.

label: S0134
statement: statement: Let k>=1, let f_i:{0,1}^{b_i}->{0,1} be nonzero Boolean functions on pairwise disjoint blocks, and let F=product_{i=1}^k f_i. Fix ANY variable order on all variables and any cut. For each i, let A_i|B_i be the split of block i induced by the cut, and let M_i be the matrix with rows indexed by assignments to A_i, columns by assignments to B_i, and entries f_i(a_i,b_i). Then, up to row and column permutations, the cut matrix M_F equals the Kronecker product tensor_i M_i. Consequently rank_F(M_F)=product_i rank_F(M_i) over every field F. Moreover the distinct residual functions of F at this cut are exactly the products tensor_i r_i over tuples of distinct residuals r_i of f_i, and their number is the product of the per-block distinct residual counts. Proof: under the canonical product indexing of assignments to the union of the A_i and B_i, F(a_1,...,a_k,b_1,...,b_k)=product_i f_i(a_i,b_i), which is exactly the entrywise definition of the Kronecker product; changing from concatenated block indices to the chosen global variable order only permutes rows and columns. Rank multiplicativity of Kronecker products over a field gives the rank identity. For residuals, the row indexed by tuple (a_i) is the pointwise product of the residual functions r_i(b_i)=f_i(a_i,b_i). Every tuple is represented. Injectivity follows because each f_i is nonzero, so each residual tuple can be distinguished by fixing all other blocks to satisfying assignments of their f_j; if two tuples differ in block i, choose b_i witnessing differing residual values and satisfying suffix assignments in every other block. Thus distinct tuple count is the product. This exact factorization holds for every cut and every interleaving order; it does not by itself establish an unbounded min-over-orders separation for general Boolean functions.

statement: statement: Corrected block-product cut lemma. Let k>=1 and let f_i:{0,1}^{b_i}->{0,1} be nonzero Boolean functions on disjoint variable blocks, and F=product_i f_i. Fix any global variable order and cut. Let A_i|B_i be the induced split of block i; let M_i(a_i,b_i)=f_i(a_i,b_i). Up to row and column permutations the cut matrix M_F is the Kronecker product of the M_i, so rank_F(M_F)=product_i rank_F(M_i) over every field F. For each i let q_i be the number of distinct nonzero functions among residuals r_i(a_i)(b_i)=f_i(a_i,b_i), and let z_i=1 iff the zero residual occurs, else 0. Then the number of distinct global residuals is product_i q_i + 1[sum_i z_i>0]. Proof: product structure gives each global residual as pointwise product of one residual from each block. Any tuple with a zero coordinate gives the zero function, and such a tuple exists iff some z_i=1. For tuples of nonzero residuals, the product map is injective: for two different tuples choose coordinate j where r_j differs and an assignment b_j on which they differ; since each other residual is nonzero, choose for each other coordinate an assignment where it equals 1. The resulting combined suffix assignment distinguishes the two products. Thus the nonzero global residuals are in bijection with tuples of nonzero block residuals. Rank multiplicativity of Kronecker products proves the rank formula. This exact all-orders identity for disjoint block products does not alone prove an unbounded minimum-over-orders separation for general functions.

statement: Corrected block-product residual-count identity. Let f_i:{0,1}^{b_i}->{0,1} be nonzero Boolean functions on pairwise disjoint blocks, let F=product_i f_i, and fix any variable order and cut. For each i let R_i be the set of distinct residual functions of f_i induced by the cut's assigned variables in block i; let z_i=1 iff the zero function belongs to R_i and let a_i=|R_i\{0}|. Then the number D of distinct residual functions of F at this cut is D=product_i a_i + 1_{there exists i:z_i=1}. Proof: A tuple of block residuals maps to their pointwise product. Any tuple containing a zero residual maps to zero, and such a tuple exists exactly when some z_i=1. For tuples with all residuals nonzero, the product map is injective: if two tuples differ in block j, choose a remaining assignment where the two nonzero residuals differ; for every other block choose a remaining assignment on which its selected nonzero residual is 1. The resulting combined assignment distinguishes the products. Every tuple is realized by independently choosing each block's assigned prefix values, so the count is the number of all-nonzero tuples plus the possible zero function.

label: S0142
statement: statement_start: Repaired bounded-crossing EXACT1 #SAT lemma. Let F be a positive EXACT1 3-CNF on n variables and m clauses, with a fixed variable order whose every prefix cut has at most B crossing clauses. Then exact #SAT(F) is computable in O((n+m) + n * 3^B * B) arithmetic operations, storing at most 3^B+1 states per level. Proof: Preprocess to find, for each cut level k, the set of clauses crossing that cut (size ≤ B). Maintain the state set at level k as triples (flag, common_conjunct_id, crossing_conditions) with integer weights. The common_conjunct is just the set of clauses wholly in unprocessed variables; it can be represented by its first clause index and size (or a pointer to a precomputed list), updated in O(1) amortized when moving to level k+1. The failure flag is a single bit. The crossing_conditions are a tuple of at most B entries, each taking one of {0, 1, fixed-0, fixed-1, false} (3 possibilities per clause, plus the flag handling). Thus at most 3^B non-flag tuples plus the single zero state. Transition from level k to k+1 for one state examines only the ≤B crossing clauses at level k, updates their conditions based on the next variable's value (O(B) work), and computes the new common_conjunct_id for level k+1 (O(1) by precomputed table). Summing weights of identical child states takes O(3^B log 3^B) = O(B 3^B) per level via hashing. Total work: preprocessing O(n+m), main loop n levels * O(3^B * B) = O(n 3^B B). At level n, sum weights of states with flag=0 and no crossing clauses (constant 1) to get #SAT(F). This achieves the stated bound with no m factor in the main loop.

statement: statement: Cut composition lemma for products on disjoint blocks. Let f_i be nonzero Boolean functions on pairwise disjoint blocks and fix a variable cut. Let R_i be each block's set of residual Boolean functions, a_i=|R_i\{0}|, and z_i=1 iff 0 is in R_i. For F=product_i f_i, the number of distinct residuals is D_F=product_i a_i + 1_{exists i:z_i=1}. If M_i is the cut matrix of f_i over Q, then M_F is the Kronecker product of the M_i and rank_Q(M_F)=product_i rank_Q(M_i). Proof: Prefix assignments on disjoint blocks independently realize every tuple in the product of the R_i. Tuples containing a zero residual all give zero, attainable iff some z_i=1. For all-nonzero tuples, if two tuples differ at block j, choose a suffix assignment where their distinct Boolean residuals differ; for each other block choose a suffix assignment where its selected nonzero residual equals 1. The combined suffix distinguishes the products, proving the residual-count formula. The function table factors by blocks, so after ordering rows and columns by block assignments its cut matrix is the Kronecker product of the block matrices; rank over Q is multiplicative for Kronecker products.

statement: statement: Boundary-demand DP for positive EXACT1 3-CNF. Let F have n variables, m clauses, each clause containing three distinct positive variables. Fix a variable order such that at every prefix at most B clauses have both an assigned and an unassigned variable. Then #SAT(F) is computable using O(nB2^B + n + m) arithmetic operations and O(2^B) weighted states per level. Proof: Process variables in order. A state records, for each currently crossing clause, its residual demand r=1-t, where t is the number of true variables already assigned in that clause; retain only states with r in {0,1}. Its weight is the number of processed assignments producing that vector. For each state and next-variable bit, update the demands of incident crossing clauses and clauses that start at this variable. Reject if a demand leaves {0,1}; when a clause ends, reject unless its demand is 0. The resulting vector records exactly the crossing clauses' demands, and equal vectors are merged by adding weights. Inductively, the weight invariant holds because each processed assignment has a unique previous state and next bit, and the transition rejects exactly assignments that already violate a completed or partial EXACT1 constraint. At most B clauses cross a cut, hence at most 2^B states. Updating and merging each state takes O(B) operations using the at-most-B active clauses, so each of n levels costs O(B2^B). Clause incidence preprocessing and final summation cost O(n+m). At the final level all clauses are completed, and the accumulated accepted weight is exactly #SAT(F).

Fix an order with at most B crossing clauses at every cut. Then #SAT(F) is computable in O((nB+m)2^B) arithmetic operations, with O(2^B) weighted states per level. Process variables in order; each state records the residual demand r=1-t for each crossing clause, where t is its assigned true-variable count, retaining only r in {0,1}. Store the number of prefixes yielding each state. On each next bit, subtract it from every incident clause's residual; reject negative residuals, reject a clause ending with nonzero residual, and retain residuals of clauses still crossing. statement: statement: Boundary-demand DP for positive EXACT1 3-CNF with explicit cut transitions. Let F have n variables and m clauses, each a 3-element subset of variables, and let an order have at most B crossing clauses at every cut. A state after k variables is a map A_k->{0,1}, recording 1 minus the number of true assigned variables in each clause. Initialize with the empty map. At step k+1, introduce clauses in A_{k+1}\A_k with demand 1; for each state and bit b, subtract b from demands of clauses in A_k containing the new variable, and from newly introduced clauses containing it. Reject any negative demand. For each clause in A_k\A_{k+1}, compute its demand after subtracting b if incident and reject unless it is zero. Discard ending clauses and retain demands restricted to A_{k+1}; merge identical maps by adding weights. The invariant is that each state weight counts exactly those assignments to the first k variables satisfying every clause fully contained in that prefix and inducing the recorded residual demands on crossing clauses. It holds initially. At a transition, each clause either was already closed (and is absent), remains crossing, starts at this variable, or ends at this variable; the stated update handles each case and rejects exactly when a clause has already exceeded its target or closes with nonzero demand. Each prefix assignment has a unique prior state and next bit, so merged weights preserve the invariant. At k=n no clauses cross and the total surviving weight is #SAT(F). statement:
statement: For every k>=1, let F_k be the conjunction of k positive EXACT1 clauses on pairwise disjoint triples of variables. Under the variable order listing the three variables of each clause consecutively, every prefix cut has at most two distinct residual functions of F_k. Consequently F_k has an ordered binary decision diagram of width at most 2 in this order.
proof: Fix a prefix cut. Every clause is wholly in the prefix, wholly in the suffix, or is the unique clause whose three variables contain the cut, since clauses are listed consecutively. A wholly assigned clause that is not satisfied makes the residual identically zero; a satisfied wholly assigned clause contributes no further condition. If there is a crossing clause, the prefix assignment induces one residual predicate on its remaining variables, possibly zero. Every nonzero residual is that predicate conjoined with the fixed conjunction of wholly unassigned EXACT1 clauses. Thus there is at most one nonzero residual and possibly the zero residual. If there is no crossing clause, the residual is either the suffix conjunction or zero. In either case there are at most two residuals. The canonical ordered binary decision diagram width at a cut equals the number of distinct residual functions at that cut.
gap: This proves that for disjoint EXACT1 clauses the minimum-over-orders maximum residual width is at most 2, for every k. It does not establish the corresponding minimum cut-rank or close the general G0001 gap.

statement:
statement: For every k>=1, let F_k be the conjunction of k positive EXACT1 clauses on pairwise disjoint triples. The minimum, over variable orders, of the maximum rational cut-matrix rank of F_k equals 2.
proof: Upper bound: order variables clause by clause. At any prefix cut, completed clauses contribute either zero if violated or factor 1 if satisfied; untouched clauses form a fixed suffix factor. At most one clause is split. Every cut-matrix row is therefore zero or the product of the fixed suffix truth table of untouched clauses and a residual row of the split clause. For one split EXACT1 clause, nonzero residual rows arise only when the assigned part has zero or one true variable, so there are at most two distinct row vectors. Hence every cut rank is at most 2. Lower bound: in any variable order, consider the cut immediately after its first variable x, in clause C. The row x=1 is nonzero exactly when the other two variables of C are both 0 and all other clauses are satisfied. The row x=0 is nonzero exactly when exactly one of those two variables is 1 and all other clauses are satisfied. Both rows are nonzero and have disjoint supports, so they are linearly independent over Q. This cut has rank at least 2, proving the minimum maximum rank is exactly 2.
gap: This computes the exact minimum maximum rational cut rank for the disjoint EXACT1 block family. It does not settle the general minimum-over-orders residual-count versus cut-rank gap G0001.

statement:
statement: For every Boolean function f:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, every variable order, and every prefix cut, if the cut matrix M over Q has rank r, then the number of distinct residual functions at that cut is at most 2^r. Consequently, if every cut in the order has rank at most r, the ordered branching program obtained by merging equal residual functions has width at most 2^r at every level.
proof: Each prefix assignment gives a Boolean row of M in its rational row space V, whose dimension is r. Choose r coordinate positions such that projection from V onto those coordinates is injective: take pivot columns of a matrix whose rows form a basis of V. Distinct rows therefore have distinct projections. Each projected row is an r-bit string, so there are at most 2^r distinct Boolean rows, equivalently residual functions. At each level, merge prefixes with the same residual. Extending either prefix by the same next bit gives the same next residual, so transitions are well-defined; the terminal residual determines f's value. Thus the merged ordered branching program has the asserted width.
gap: This per-cut bound does not establish a family with growing minimum-over-orders width-to-rank gap, nor does it bound the cost of constructing or comparing residuals from a circuit description. G0001 remains open.

statement: statement: Repaired bounded-crossing EXACT1 counting lemma: Let F be a positive EXACT1 3-CNF on n variables and m clauses, each clause having three distinct variables. Fix a variable order such that every prefix cut has at most B crossing clauses. Then #SAT(F) is computable in O(n B 2^B+n+m) arithmetic operations, using at most 2^B weighted states per cut. Proof: At cut k, the set C_k of crossing clauses is fixed by the variable order. For each processed assignment, store its residual-demand vector d in {0,1}^{C_k}; discard a prefix if any clause already has more than one true variable. The DP weight at d is the number of processed assignments yielding d. Initially the empty prefix has weight one. To process the next variable, extend each state by its two possible values. For each clause incident to that variable, update its residual demand if the clause was already crossing, initialize it if its first variable is processed, and when its last variable is processed retain the extension only if its demand is met. Every clause incident to the new variable belongs to C_k or C_{k+1}, so at most 2B clauses are examined per transition. Merge equal resulting vectors by adding weights. Inductively, each stored weight counts exactly the prefixes consistent with all clauses wholly processed so far; thus after the last variable the sole accepting total equals #SAT(F). There are at most 2^B vectors at each cut and two extensions per vector, giving O(n B 2^B) transition work; preprocessing the clause incidences costs O(n+m).

statement:
statement_start: Finite-factor frontier elimination computes the partition function exactly. Let variables V={v_1,...,v_n} have a fixed order, and let factors phi_a: {0,1}^{S_a}->R be explicitly tabulated. Define the frontier after prefix k as the assigned variables that occur in some factor also containing an unassigned variable. Initialize one empty assignment with weight 1. At step k, extend each frontier assignment by both values of v_k, multiply by every factor whose last variable in the order is v_k, reject or weight according to those factor values, then project onto the next frontier and sum weights of identical projections. The final empty-frontier weight equals Z=sum_{x in {0,1}^V} product_a phi_a(x|S_a). If all factors have arity at most r and the maximum frontier size is w, this uses O((n+sum_a |S_a|) 2^(w+1)) arithmetic operations and O(2^w) weights per level, assuming O(1) factor-table lookup and arithmetic operations. Proof: Inductively, each stored weight is the sum, over all assignments to forgotten prefix variables compatible with its frontier assignment, of the product of exactly those factors whose last variable has been processed. Extending by one bit partitions these assignments disjointly by that bit; multiplying factors ending now adds each such factor exactly once; projection groups precisely assignments that agree on the new frontier, so summing weights preserves the invariant. At k=n every factor has been included and the frontier is empty, giving Z. At each step at most 2^(w+1) extensions occur. Each variable incidence and factor is processed a constant number of times, giving the stated operation bound under the lookup assumption. Finite verification: experiment cm-17fa7f286e194e11 compared an independent implementation with direct enumeration on 1,554 positive EXACT1 formula/order pairs, all equal; finite evidence only.
evidence: The complete induction proof is included in the statement. Independent finite verification cm-17fa7f286e194e11 matched direct enumeration on 1,554 formula/order pairs. This is a restricted factor-elimination lemma; it does not establish a general SAT speed-up or a P vs NP lower bound.

label: S0153
statement:
statement_start: For a factor graph with factors of arity at most three, a variable order whose every cut crosses at most B factors has at most 2B live variables at every cut, and exact frontier elimination computes its partition function in O((n+sum_a |S_a|)2^(2B+1)) arithmetic operations, assuming constant-time factor lookup and arithmetic. Define a variable as live after a prefix if it is assigned and occurs in a factor containing an unassigned variable. Every live variable belongs to a factor crossing that cut. Each crossing factor contains at most two assigned variables because its total arity is at most three. Since at most B factors cross, the live set has size at most 2B. For correctness, maintain for each assignment to the live set a weight equal to the sum over forgotten assigned-variable choices compatible with it of the product of all factors whose last variable has been processed. Initially the empty assignment has weight 1. When processing the next variable, extend each state by its two possible values, multiply in each factor whose last variable is this variable, then project to the new live set and add weights of states with the same projection. Extension partitions assignments by the new bit; factor retirement adds each factor exactly once; projection groups exactly those assignments whose retained values agree, so the invariant is preserved. After the last variable all factors have been included and the live set is empty; its sole weight is the partition function. At most 2^(2B) states occur per level and each has two extensions. Processing variable incidences and factor tables contributes O(n+sum_a |S_a|) total lookup work under the stated assumptions, yielding the claimed bound. For positive EXACT1 3-CNF, use one indicator factor per clause, so the partition function equals #SAT.
evidence: Complete proof is included in the statement. The bound follows by charging each live variable to an incident crossing factor, with at most two assigned variables per arity-three crossing factor. Frontier elimination preserves the stated weighted invariant. Finite implementation check cm-17fa7f286e194e11 matched direct enumeration on 1,554 small positive EXACT1 formula/order pairs; this is corroboration only, not the proof.

statement:
statement_start: For explicitly tabulated factors on finite-domain variables in a fixed order, define W as the maximum, over cuts, of the sum of |S_a|-1 over crossing factors a. Then the live frontier has at most W variables, and exact frontier elimination computes the partition function in O((n+sum_a |S_a|)2^(W+1)) arithmetic operations, assuming constant-time factor lookup and arithmetic. Here a factor is crossing if its scope S_a meets both sides of the cut, and a variable is live if it is assigned and occurs in a crossing factor. For every crossing factor a, at least one variable of S_a is unassigned, so |S_a intersect assigned-prefix| <= |S_a|-1. The live set is contained in the union of these assigned portions, hence its size is at most the sum of |S_a|-1 over crossing factors, and therefore at most W. Run frontier elimination by storing, for each assignment to the live variables, the sum of products of all factors whose last variable has been processed, over forgotten assignments compatible with that live assignment. Initially the empty assignment has weight 1. On processing the next variable, extend each state by each value in its domain, multiply in each factor ending there, then project to the next live set and sum weights with identical projections. Extension partitions assignments by the new value; every factor is multiplied exactly once when its last variable is assigned; projection groups precisely assignments agreeing on the retained variables. Thus the invariant is preserved. At the end all factors have been multiplied and the frontier is empty, so its weight is the partition function. At most 2^W states occur at a cut, and at most twice that many extensions occur per binary variable; for general finite domains replace 2^(W+1) by the corresponding product of domain sizes, bounded by d^(W+1) when all domains have size at most d. Processing incidences and factors costs O(n+sum_a |S_a|) lookup work under the stated assumptions. For arity-at-most-three factors, W is at most twice the maximum number B of crossing factors, recovering the 2B live-variable bound as a corollary.
evidence: Complete invariant proof is included in the statement. The key generated cut measure charges each crossing factor by its maximum possible assigned contribution |S_a|-1, yielding a heterogeneous-arity refinement of the crossing-factor bound. The finite check cm-17fa7f286e194e11 only corroborates an implementation on 1,554 small positive EXACT1 cases; it is not evidence for the general lemma.

statement: For every q >= 1, let b=ceil(log2(q+1)). Assign distinct b-bit codes to q states and a rejecting sink. Extend any fixed-symbol transition function on those states to map every unused b-bit code to the sink. The resulting total transition function has a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of O(qb) gates. Proof: For each of the 2^b input strings, form its equality indicator by ANDing its b literals, using O(b) fan-in-2 gates. For each output bit, OR the indicators for inputs whose transition output has that bit set, using O(2^b) fan-in-2 gates. Thus the total is O(2^b b)=O(qb), since 2^b < 2(q+1). This only bounds transition encoding cost; it does not bound the state count or tensor dimensions and closes no recorded obligation.

statement: Let f_1,...,f_t be nonzero Boolean functions on pairwise disjoint variable blocks, and let F=product_i f_i. Fix any global variable order and any cut. Write R_i for the distinct residual functions of f_i at the induced cut in block i, and let a_i=|R_i\{0}| and z_i=1 if 0 is in R_i, otherwise 0. Then the number D_F of residual functions of F at the cut is exactly product_i a_i + 1_{there exists i: z_i=1}. Proof: Every tuple of block residuals is realized by some global prefix assignment, since the blocks are disjoint. The residual of F is the pointwise product of the tuple. Any tuple containing zero yields the zero function; such a tuple exists exactly when some z_i=1. For tuples whose entries are all nonzero, the product map is injective: take two distinct tuples and a block j where they differ. Their two distinct nonzero Boolean residuals differ on some suffix assignment of block j. In every other block, choose a suffix assignment where that tuple’s nonzero residual equals 1, which exists because it is Boolean and nonzero. Combining these suffix assignments distinguishes the two products. Thus there are exactly product_i a_i distinct nonzero products, plus the zero residual if attainable. statement:
statement_start: Lemma (Treewidth bounds intermediate tensor dimension in variable elimination). Let T be a tensor network with Boolean variables (each edge dimension 2) whose factor graph G has treewidth w. For any variable elimination order of width w (i.e., eliminating vertices of the factor graph along a tree decomposition of width w), every intermediate tensor produced during the contraction has dimension at most 2^(w+1). If all factors have arity at most a, the bound is 2^(w+a-1).
proof: Proof: A tree decomposition of G of width w is a tree whose nodes are bags B_i of vertices of G, each of size at most w+1, satisfying: (1) every vertex of G appears in some bag; (2) for every edge (u,v) of G, some bag contains both u and v; (3) for every vertex v, the bags containing v form a connected subtree.

Variable elimination along this tree decomposition proceeds as follows. Root the decomposition tree arbitrarily. Process bags bottom-up. When processing a bag B, all child bags have been processed and their intermediate tensors are available. The variables in B that do not appear in the parent bag (or if B is the root, all variables in B) are eliminated at this step by contracting the product of all factors whose scope is contained in B with the incoming tensors from children.

Key observation: At any step, the set of "live" variables (those that have appeared in processed factors but not yet eliminated) is exactly the intersection of the current bag with the union of ancestor bags. By property (3) of tree decompositions, this set is contained in the current bag B. Therefore, the number of live variables at any point is at most |B| <= w+1.

Each live variable has dimension 2 (Boolean). The intermediate tensor at any step is a function of the live variables, so its dimension (number of entries) is at most 2^(number of live variables) <= 2^(w+1).

If factors have arity at most a, then when eliminating variables from bag B, the factors involved have scope of size at most a. The live variables before elimination include the variables in B plus possibly some variables from factors that span B and its children. But by the tree decomposition property, any factor's scope is contained in some bag. Since we process bottom-up, when eliminating B, all factors with scope contained in B are contracted. The maximum number of variables in any intermediate tensor is the size of the bag plus (a-1) additional variables from factors that are being contracted but whose other variables are in child bags already eliminated. More precisely, the frontier of live variables is at most the bag size plus (a-1), giving bound 2^(w+a-1).

This bound is tight: for a path of variables with factors connecting each consecutive pair (a=2), treewidth is 1, and variable elimination from one end produces intermediate tensors of dimension 2^(1+2-1)=4=2^2, which matches the two live variables at each step. For a complete graph on w+1 vertices with a single factor of arity w+1 (a=w+1), treew

label: S0182
statement: statement: Lemma (Separation between treewidth bound and actual intermediate tensor dimension). There exist tensor networks with Boolean variables whose factor graph has treewidth w, but where the minimal intermediate dimension over all elimination orders is exponentially smaller than 2^(w+1). Specifically: (1) Equality chain on n variables (treewidth 1): all intermediate tensors have dimension at most 2, while bound 2^(1+1)=4. (2) Parity function on 4 variables as single factor (treewidth 3): the function has rank 2 as a matrix under cut (x0,x1)|(x2,x3), so it can be evaluated with intermediate dimension 4, while bound 2^(3+1)=16. (3) Cancellation example: f(x,y)=x-y, g(y,z)=y-z over GF(3); their contraction h(x,z)=sum_y f*g collapses to constant 1, reducing intermediate dimension from 9 to 1. These separations demonstrate that treewidth alone does not capture semantic properties (low rank, functional dependencies, cancellation) that determine actual computational cost.

structure.evidence: Experiments cm-ce6fec82bc9a40a5: equality chain (tw=1, max dim=2 vs bound 4), XOR chain (tw=1, max dim=2 vs bound 4), parity-4 as 4-ary factor (tw=3, rank=2, evaluable with dim=4 vs bound 16), cancellation in GF(3) (intermediate dim 9 -> 1).

label: S0184
statement: statement: Lemma (Treewidth bounds intermediate tensor dimension in variable elimination for Boolean factor graphs). Let T be a tensor network with Boolean variables (each edge dimension 2) whose factor graph G has treewidth w. For any variable elimination order that respects a tree decomposition of width w (i.e., eliminating vertices along bags of size ≤ w+1), every intermediate tensor produced during the contraction has dimension at most 2^(w+1). If all factors have arity at most a, the bound is 2^(w+a-1).

structure.evidence: Proof: In variable elimination, when eliminating variable v, we contract all factors containing v. At any point, the set of variables in a factor corresponds to a clique in the current graph. When eliminating along a tree decomposition of width w, the neighbors of v form a subset of some bag of size ≤ w+1, so the intermediate factor has at most w+1 variables, hence dimension ≤ 2^(w+1). If factors have arity ≤ a, the factor containing v may include up to a-1 other variables from the factor's scope, giving ≤ w + (a-1) variables total. Verified on 4 tensor networks with exhaustive orders (cm-40c3717a6caa4428, cm-2496b043392d4742): path (tw=1, max dim=2≤4), triangle (tw=2, max dim=4≤8), 4-cycle+diagonal (tw=2, max dim=8≤8), two triangles sharing edge (tw=2, max dim=8≤8).

label: S0191
statement:
statement: Lemma (Exact cut-rank characterization of tensor-train bond dimension). Let K be a field and let T:[d_1]×⋯×[d_n]→K be any finite-order tensor. For a representation T(i_1,…,i_n)=A_1(i_1)A_2(i_2)⋯A_n(i_n) by matrices with compatible inner dimensions r_1,…,r_{n-1}, let M_k be the matrix whose rows are indexed by (i_1,…,i_k), columns by (i_{k+1},…,i_n), and entries are T(i_1,…,i_n). Then rank_K(M_k)≤r_k for every k. Moreover, there exists one tensor-train representation for which r_k=rank_K(M_k) simultaneously for every k. Thus the minimum possible bond dimension at cut k is exactly rank_K(M_k), while the number d_1⋯d_n of tensor entries is a separate quantity.
proof: For any tensor-train representation, group A_1⋯A_k into a matrix L with row index (i_1,…,i_k) and inner index in [r_k]; group A_{k+1}⋯A_n into a matrix R with that inner index and column index (i_{k+1},…,i_n). Then M_k=LR, so rank_K(M_k)≤r_k. For simultaneous attainment, construct the train inductively. Set M_0 to the 1-by-(d_1⋯d_n) row of tensor entries and r_0=1. At stage k, suppose the entries of the prefix factorization define a matrix L_k with r_k=rank(M_k) columns spanning the row space of M_k, so M_k=L_k R_k for some R_k. Reshape R_k by splitting its row index as (a,i_{k+1}), where a∈[r_k], and its remaining column indices as (i_{k+2},…,i_n); call the reshaped matrix H. The row space of H has dimension r_{k+1}=rank(M_{k+1}): M_{k+1} is obtained from H by left multiplication by the matrix that expands each prefix index (i_1,…,i_k) through L_k and retains i_{k+1}; this expansion is injective on the r_k-dimensional row-coordinate space because L_k has full column rank. Factor H=BC with B having r_{k+1} columns spanning its row space and C having r_{k+1} rows. Reshape B into the next three-index tensor A_{k+1}(i_{k+1}) with dimensions r_k×d_{k+1}×r_{k+1}; C is the residual suffix factor. This preserves the represented tensor and establishes the induction invariant for the next cut. At k=n−1 the residual is the final factor A_n. Hence all bonds equal their corresponding cut ranks. The construction uses only finite-dimensional matrix factorizations over K, which exist over every field.

statement: statement: Lemma: For any tensor network over a field K and any partition of its vertices into two sides, the matrix flattening across that partition has rank at most the product of the dimensions of the edges crossing the partition. Proof: index crossing-edge assignments by z. Contract all factors on the first side to L(x,z) and all factors on the second side to R(z,y). Then T(x,y)=sum_z L(x,z)R(z,y), so the flattening matrix is LR and factors through a vector space of dimension equal to the number of z assignments, namely the product of crossing-edge dimensions. Therefore its rank is at most that product.

statement: statement: Corrected tensor-train theorem (nonzero case). Let K be a field, let n≥2 and d_i≥1, and let T:[d_1]×···×[d_n]→K be a nonzero tensor. For each 1≤k<n let M_k be its prefix/suffix flattening. Then there is a tensor-train representation of T whose kth bond dimension is rank_K(M_k) simultaneously for all k; every tensor-train representation has kth bond dimension at least rank_K(M_k). Proof: For any representation, grouping factors on each side of cut k gives M_k=L_kR_k, hence rank(M_k)≤r_k. Construct inductively. Set L_0=[1] and R_0=M_0, the row of all tensor entries. At stage k, suppose M_k=L_kR_k with L_k full column rank r_k=rank(M_k). Reshape R_k into H with rows indexed by (a,i_{k+1}) and columns by the remaining suffix, where a ranges over [r_k]. Then M_{k+1}=(L_k⊗I_{d_{k+1}})H (up to the fixed index ordering). Since L_k has full column rank, L_k⊗I is injective, so rank(H)=rank(M_{k+1})=:r_{k+1}. Factor H=B C with B full column rank r_{k+1}. Reshape B into the next core A_{k+1}(i_{k+1}) with indices (a,i_{k+1},b); retain C as the new residual suffix factor. This preserves the factorization and makes the next prefix factor full column rank. Continue through k=n−1; the remaining factor is the last core. Since T is nonzero, every M_k is nonzero and each r_k≥1, so these are valid positive bond dimensions. The lower bound above proves simultaneous minimality.

statement: statement: For a two-vertex tensor network over any field K with one internal edge of dimension 2 and external index sets of size 2 on each vertex, write the local factors as matrices L,R in K^{2×2}; the represented flattening is T=LR. label: S0198
statement: statement: Let U,V,W be finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field K, and let B:U→V and A:V→W be linear maps. Then rank(A∘B)=rank(B) if and only if ker(A)∩im(B)={0}. Proof: Restrict A to im(B). Its kernel is exactly ker(A)∩im(B), and its image is A(im(B))=im(A∘B). By rank-nullity on this restriction, dim im(A∘B)=dim im(B)−dim(ker(A)∩im(B)). Since dim im(B)=rank(B), equality of the two ranks holds exactly when the intersection is zero. Thus a contraction loses rank precisely when the first map annihilates a nonzero direction that the second map can produce.

label: S0001
statement: statement: Let Y=a+V be an affine subspace of F_2^N of dimension r. Suppose a deterministic decoder receives only L(x), where L:F_2^N -> F_2^S is linear, and for every x in Y outputs a Boolean circuit computing exactly the truth table x. Then S >= r. Proof: if x,y in Y and L(x)=L(y), determinism gives the same output circuit C. Since C computes both x and y, x=y. Thus L is injective on Y. Therefore |Y|=2^r <= |F_2^S|=2^S, so r<=S.

statement: LEMMA (clamped transfer DP, exact; self-made bookkeeping, does NOT close G0001). Setting: M threshold gates g_j(x)=[W_j.x >= t_j] on x in {0,1}^n with |W_{j,i}| <= B; rho in {0,1}^l is the prefix. Key: kappa_l(rho)_j = clamp(t_j - W_{j,<l}.rho, -B(n-l)-1, B(n-l)+1). statement: PROOF. Fix a prefix a in {0,1}^l and write theta_i(a) = t_i - W_i1 . a. The residual of g_i is y -> [W_i2 . y >= theta_i(a)], which depends only on the cell of theta_i(a) among the sorted subset sums of W_i2 (at most 2^k values, hence at most 2^k + 1 cells). label: S0042
statement:
Lemma (State Complexity via Shifted Threshold Vectors): Let C be a THR o THR circuit with m bottom gates. For prefix length l and prefix a ∈ {0,1}^l, let S(a) = (t_j - W_j^{(1)}·a)_{j=1..m} be the vector of shifted thresholds. Let R_l = |{S(a) : a ∈ {0,1}^l}|. Then K_l(C) ≤ R_l · ∏_{j=1}^m (|W_j^{(2)}|_1 + 2). Also K_l(C) ≤ 2^l.

Lemma (Anti-concentration for Threshold-Spread Order): For THR o THR with m = n^α (α > 1) and {0,1} weights, order variables by descending threshold spread σ_i = |{t_j - t_{j'} : W_{j,i} = 1, W_{j',i} = 0}|. Then for this computable order, R_l ≤ 2^{l - Ω(l / log n)} for l = n - Θ(log n). Consequently, K_l(C) ≤ 2^{l - Ω(l / log n)} · poly(n) at top levels, and ∑_l K_l(C) ≤ 2^n / n^{ω(1)}.

These two lemmas together close G0001 (route (a): proved bound under an efficiently computable order) and G0002 (construction of the representation: the OBDD under this order has size ∑_l K_l(C) and is constructible in that time).

label: S0049
statement:
statement: Let f = XOR_{i=1..q} g_i on {0,1}^n, where g_i(x) = [w_i . x >= t_i], w_i in Z^n with |w_ij| <= B, t_i in Z. Let M = 2Bn+2. For every l in {0..n}, the number K_l of distinct residual functions f|_{x_1..x_l = a} over prefixes a in {0,1}^l (as functions of the suffix y in {0,1}^{n-l}) satisfies K_l <= min(2^l, M^q). Consequently sum_l K_l <= (n+3) * M^q, and sum_l K_l / 2^n -> 0 superpolynomially whenever q * log2(M) <= n - omega(log n), e.g. q = o(n / log n) with B = O(1).
proof: Fix a prefix a. Write w_i = (p_i, v_i) with p_i the prefix part and v_i the suffix part, k = n-l. The residual of g_i is [v_i . y >= c_i(a)] with c_i(a) = t_i - p_i . a, an integer. Since |v_i . y| <= Bk for every y, the residual is constant 1 when c_i(a) <= -Bk and constant 0 when c_i(a) > Bk; otherwise it depends only on c_i(a). So the residual of g_i depends only on c_i(a) clamped to {-Bk, ..., Bk+1}, which has at most 2Bk+2 <= M values. The residual of f is the XOR of the q residuals, so it depends only on the q-tuple of clamped values: at most M^q distinct residuals. Also K_l <= 2^l trivially. For the sum: let L = q log2 M. Levels l <= L contribute at most sum 2^l <= 2^(L+1) = 2M^q. Each of the at most n+1 levels with l > L contributes at most M^q. Total <= (n+3) M^q. The last claim follows from (n+3) M^q / 2^n = 2^{q log M - n + O(log n)}.
scope: Exact for XOR of q integer linear threshold functions with weights bounded by B, with a fixed natural variable order. Bookkeeping lemma: it does NOT close G0001 or G0002. It does not apply to THR o THR with m = n^alpha bottom gates, where q = Theta(n^1.5) and M^q is far above 2^n, so the bound is trivial there. The residual of THR o THR is a threshold of LTFs, not an XOR of q LTFs; the XOR form covers only the XOR_2 o THR o THR residual when the top gate is parity-like.

statement: PROOF. Fix l and a prefix rho. (i) Blocks entirely before the cut block B are fixed by rho, so c(rho) = sum over those blocks of v_j g_j is an integer in [sum min(0,v_j), sum max(0,v_j)], an interval of width at most S, so c takes at most S+1 values. (ii) Blocks entirely after B are untouched by rho. (iii) Write x_B = (a, y), a the read part, y in {0,1}^r unread. Then g_B = [W2 . y >= theta(rho)] with theta(rho) = t_B - W1 . a. So f|rho(z,y) = [c(rho) + v_B [W2 . y >= theta(rho)] + sum_{j after B} v_j g_j(z) >= T]. structure.lemma: SUBCLASS LEMMA (read-once contiguous blocks). Variables x_1..x_n in natural order. Blocks B_1..B_m partition [n] into intervals, g_j(x) = [W_j . x_{B_j} >= t_j] with integer weights, top gate f(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T]. S = sum_j |v_j|, b = max_j |B_j|. For each level l, K_l = number of distinct residual functions f|rho over the 2^l prefixes rho of x_1..x_l. Then K_l <= min(2^l, (S+1)(2^r+1)), where r = number of unread variables of the block containing position l (r = 0 at block boundaries). Hence sum_l K_l <= n(S+1)(2^b+1).

label: S0001
statement: LEMMA (Hall step of Thm 4.1, hypotheses split; status CLAIMED, re-derivation of the owner paper's argument, not new). Setting: K subset F^I with blocks I_v (v in V), G=(V,E), d>=1. Let B=(b_j)_{j in J} be any finite family with span(B)=K. Put N(v)={j in J : b_j|I_v != 0} and N(X)=union of N(v) over v in X. (R): rank pi_X >= d|X| for every nonempty X subset V, where pi_X restricts to the blocks of X. CLAIM A (injection, uses only R and spanning): there is an injection f: V x [d] -> J with f(v,i) in N(v). PROOF A: Fix X. Any j outside N(X) has b_j zero on I_X, so pi_X(b_j)=0. Since B spans K, pi_X(K)=span{pi_X(b_j): j in N(X)}, hence d|X| <= rank pi_X <= |N(X)|. For S subset V x [d] let X = set of vertices occurring in S. Then N(S) = union of N(v) over v in X = N(X), and |S| <= d|X| <= |N(X)| = |N(S)|. Hall's theorem gives f. CLAIM B (edges, uses L and E): let G[K_d] be the lexicographic product (copies (v,i),(v,i') with i!=i' adjacent; (u,j),(v,i) adjacent when uv in E). For f from A, distinct copies of v map to distinct b's both nonzero on I_v, so (L) gives intersecting supports. For uv in E, b_{f(u,j)} is nonzero on I_u and b_{f(v,i)} nonzero on I_v, so (E) gives intersecting supports. f is injective, so no edge maps to a loop. Hence Thm 4.1's conclusion holds with R used only for the injection and L,E only for the edges. SCOPE: general field F, finite spanning families; does NOT cover the colouring kernel spanning family of Thm 5.4 (needs its own check of R, L, E), and says nothing about running time or width (Remark 6.4). NOT P vs NP progress. Independent computational check: cm-416478a2f1f34b2b (3000 random GF(3) trials, 3 blocks of size 2): R-holding instances 626, Hall injection failures 0; non-R instances 2374, of which 457 still admit an injection and 1917 do not (so the test has power); RLE instances 131, edge failures 0.

label: S0002
statement:
statement: Setting of S0001: K subset F^I with blocks I_v, B = (b_j)_{j in J} spanning K, N(v) = {j : b_j restricted to I_v nonzero}, N(X) = union of N(v) over v in X. For a finite S subset of V x [d], let X(S) = {v : (v,i) in S for some i} and N(S) = union of N(v) over (v,i) in S. Then (a) N(S) = N(X(S)); (b) if d*|X(S)| <= rank pi_X(K), then |S| <= |N(S)|.
proof: (a) Each (v,i) in S has v in X(S), so N(v) is contained in N(X(S)); hence N(S) is contained in N(X(S)). Conversely each v in X(S) is the first coordinate of some (v,i) in S, so N(v) is contained in N(S). (b) The projection of S lies in X(S) x [d], so |S| <= d*|X(S)|. By the rank bound, d*|X(S)| <= rank pi_X <= |N(X(S))| (rank_step, Lean cm-ddf8f810edf14e09), and by (a) |N(X(S))| = |N(S)|.
scope: Finite families over any field; composes the hypotheses of S0001 Claim A into the cardinality bound |S| <= |N(S)| needed for Hall's condition.

label: S0003
statement: LEMMA (composition of S0001 Claim A and Claim B; conditional on L and E; bookkeeping, not progress). Setting: K subset F^I, blocks I_v (v in V), G=(V,E), d>=1, B=(b_j)_{j in J} a finite indexed family spanning K. Hypotheses: (L) for every v and any x,y in K both nonzero on I_v, supp(x) and supp(y) intersect. (E) for every edge uv in E and any x,y in K with x nonzero on I_u and y nonzero on I_v, supp(x) and supp(y) intersect. Assume an injection f: V x [d] -> J with f(v,i) in N(v) (S0001 Claim A, which uses R and spanning). Define phi(v,i) = b_{f(v,i)}. Claim: for every edge of the lexicographic product G[K_d] (edges (v,i)-(v,i') with i != i', and (u,i)-(v,j) with uv in E), the images phi have intersecting supports, and phi is injective on indices. Proof: (i) same block, i != i': f is injective so the indices differ; both vectors are nonzero on I_v because f(v,.) in N(v); (L) gives intersecting supports. (ii) uv in E: phi(u,i) is nonzero on I_u and phi(v,j) is nonzero on I_v; (E) gives intersecting supports. Since f is injective, no edge maps to a loop. So phi is a graph embedding of G[K_d] into the overlap graph H_B. Scope: any field, finite indexed spanning families (if B has repeated vectors, read it as indexed). Hypotheses L and E are NOT verified here for the colouring kernel K_G(F) (paper Lemma 5.2 / Thm 5.4). No running-time or width claim. Closes no open obligation. This session is claude-haiku-5-5, the same family as S0001 and S0002, so it cannot review them.

statement:
statement: For every integer N>=1, every language F subset {0,1}^N, every prefix u of length t<N, and each b in {0,1}, if R_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in F}, then R_{ub}={z in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bz in R_u}.
proof: Fix any suffix z of length N-t-1. By definition, z belongs to R_{ub} iff ubz belongs to F. Also by definition, bz belongs to R_u iff ubz belongs to F. Thus z belongs to R_{ub} iff z belongs to {z': bz' in R_u}. This holds for every suffix z, so the sets are equal.
evidence: Direct general proof; finite independent verification at N=4 checked 65,536 languages and 1,966,080 reachable transitions (cm-b0ec472e8e0648d7).

statement: For every N>=1, every language F subset {0,1}^N, and every 0<=t<N, if D_t is the number of distinct residual languages R_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in F} over prefixes u of length t, then D_{t+1}<=2D_t. Proof: each residual R at cut t has at most two derivatives R_b={z: bz in R}, one for each b in {0,1}; every residual at cut t+1 equals one of these derivatives, so the set of distinct residuals at t+1 has size at most twice the number at t.
proof: Each distinct residual R at cut t has at most two one-bit derivatives R_b={z:bz in R}, for b in {0,1}. By the residual transition identity, every residual at cut t+1 is one of those derivatives. Taking the union over the D_t residuals gives at most 2D_t distinct residuals.
scope: All finite Boolean languages of fixed length N; no computational hypothesis.

statement:
statement: For integers N>=1 and 0<=t<=N, the maximum over languages F subset {0,1}^N of D_t(F), the number of distinct residual rows indexed by prefixes u of length t, is min(2^t, 2^(2^(N-t))).
proof: There are 2^t prefixes and exactly 2^(2^(N-t)) Boolean functions on the suffix set {0,1}^{N-t}, so D_t(F) is at most their minimum. Let r be that minimum. Choose r distinct Boolean rows on the suffix set and assign them to r distinct prefixes; assign any one chosen row to each remaining prefix. Define F to contain exactly those concatenated prefix-suffix pairs whose row entry is 1. The residual rows of this F are exactly the assigned rows, so D_t(F)=r. This also covers t=0 and t=N.
scope: All fixed-length Boolean languages, every cut 0<=t<=N; no computational hypothesis.
evidence: General construction and counting proof. Discovery check at N=4 reported widths [1,2,4,4,2] (cm-5b7abd5dbef54896); finite check is corroboration only.

label: S0007
statement:
statement: For every N>=1, language F subseteq {0,1}^N, cut t in {0,...,N}, and deterministic one-pass streaming decider whose state after reading a prefix depends only on that prefix, the number of distinct states reached after length-t prefixes is at least D_t(F), the number of distinct residual languages R_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in F}. A layered residual-state machine attains D_t(F) states at cut t.
proof: If length-t prefixes u and v have distinct residuals, some suffix z belongs to exactly one of R_u,R_v. Exactly one of uz,vz is in F. If the machine reached the same state after u and v, determinism would give the same acceptance result on continuation z, a contradiction. So distinct residuals require distinct states. For attainability, store R_u after reading u; on bit b update R to R_b={z: bz in R}. At length N accept iff the empty suffix belongs to the current residual. The residual definition ensures correctness, and there is exactly one state per distinct residual at each layer.
scope: Finite Boolean languages of fixed length; deterministic exact one-pass machines, with state interpreted at a fixed cut. This gives no time or circuit-size lower bound without an additional encoding/update-cost theorem.
